brief_summary: Pulse oximeters estimate arterial oxyhaemoglobin saturation (SaO₂) from photoplethysmographic signals recorded at peripheral sites (usually the fingertip), thus measuring the peripheral oxygen saturation (SpO₂). They are ubiquitous in emergency medicine because they offer a non-invasive, continuous measure of oxygenation and can alert clinicians to impending hypoxaemia, both during procedures such as rapid sequence intubation or sedation, or for continuous monitoring of patients. However, the accuracy of SpO₂ is often assumed to be instantaneous. This assumption is particularly hazardous during critical events involving rapid desaturation and resaturation. In such situations clinicians use SpO₂ readings to decide when to stop an apnea period during laryngoscopy and commence reoxygenation. If there is a delay between actual arterial desaturation and the displayed SpO₂, the clinician may not recognise hypoxaemia in time or may resume ventilation too late.
lead_sponsor: Cliniques universitaires Saint-Luc- Université Catholique de Louvain
primary_outcomes: Evaluation of SpO₂ Resaturation Following Voluntary Apnea
title: Temporal Dynamics of Peripheral SpO₂ During Reoxygenation

brief_summary:
The goal of this observational study is to learn whether implementing evidence-based strategies in cardiology practices can improve guideline-recommended low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) management in adults at high risk for cardiovascular disease. Participants include adults with a recent myocardial infarction (heart attack), coronary stent placement, percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), ischemic heart disease, or a coronary artery calcium (CAC) score of 300 or higher. The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Do implementation strategies increase the proportion of patients who receive LDL-C testing, have lipid-lowering therapy (LLT) started or intensified, and achieve guideline-recommended LDL-C goals within 6 months of their index visit?
* Do implementation strategies improve cardiovascular risk factor management and LDL-C goal attainment at 3 and 12 months after the index visit?
* How acceptable, feasible, and effective are these implementation strategies for patients, clinicians, and healthcare sites? Researchers will compare outcomes among patients receiving care after implementation of the study strategies with outcomes from a retrospective cohort of similar patients treated before the strategies were introduced.

Participants will:

* Receive usual cardiovascular care from their healthcare providers.
* Be cared for at sites implementing one or more evidence-based strategies, which may include clinician performance scorecards, electronic health record best practice alerts, clinician education, patient education, and/or follow-up through an Advanced Practice Provider (APP) care pathway.
* Attend routine follow-up visits and undergo LDL-C testing and other cardiovascular assessments as part of standard clinical care.
* Have information from their electronic health records reviewed, including laboratory results, medications, blood pressure measurements, smoking status, and cardiovascular outcomes.
* Complete surveys about their experiences with the implementation strategies, if applicable.
* Be followed for up to 12 months after their index visit.
primary_outcomes: Binary indicator of LDL-C <55 mg/dL for patients with a recent MI or coronary stent and <70 mg/dL for patients undergoing PCI with no MI and/or ischemic heart disease or with a CAC score of at least 300 at 6-month post visit, with time to event.
Binary indicator of patients who received LDL-C testing, with time to event.
Binary indicator of patients in whom lipid lowering therapy was initiated/intensified within the first six months after index event.
title: Improving Implementation of Guideline-Recommended LDL-C Management in High-Risk Cardiovascular Patients

brief_summary:
This is a single-center, single-arm phase II clinical study designed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of Iparomlimab and Tuvonralimab combined with cetuximab in patients with locally advanced resectable oral squamous cell carcinoma.

The treatment regimen for the experimental group is as follows:

The recommended dose of epalorestivolimab is 5 mg/kg. Cetuximab is administered at an initial dose of 400 mg/m² followed by 250 mg/m² once weekly, or alternatively cetuximab 500 mg/m² once every 2 weeks, via intravenous infusion. Each treatment cycle lasts 21 days, with 3 cycles administered preoperatively. Patients will undergo surgical resection at 3 weeks ± 7 days after completion of neoadjuvant therapy, followed by concurrent radiotherapy or chemoradiotherapy at 6 weeks ± 2 weeks postoperatively.

One clinical tumor imaging assessment will be performed preoperatively per RECIST v1.1 (Appendix 4). In addition, clinically required assessments including vital signs, physical examination, complete blood count, urinalysis, liver and renal function tests, serum electrolytes, thyroid function, electrocardiogram, ECOG performance status, and quality-of-life questionnaires will be completed on Day 1 of each treatment cycle (refer to the study flowchart for specific assessments at each visit). Subjects with hepatitis virus carriage will have viral load monitoring every 2 to 4 treatment cycles.

If PD is assessed per RECIST v1.1 but the subject remains clinically stable or the investigator judges that continued treatment may still benefit the subject, reassessment may be performed 4 weeks later using irRECIST. Treatment may be continued if no progressive disease is identified on reassessment.
interventions: iparomlimab and tuvonralimab combined with cetuximab

title: Iparomlimab and Tuvonralimab With With Cetuximab in Resectable OSCC

brief_summary:
The BECOME trial will study whether becotatug vedotin combined with pucotenlimab can shrink tumors and how safe this treatment is in adults with colorectal cancer that has returned or spread after at least two prior lines of standard treatment. The study described in the informed consent form is for patients whose tumors test positive for a protein called epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR).

Becotatug vedotin, also known as MRG003, is an antibody-drug conjugate (ADC). It combines an antibody that recognizes EGFR with a drug designed to kill cancer cells. Pucotenlimab is an immunotherapy that blocks a protein called PD-1 and may help the immune system recognize and attack cancer cells. The benefit and risks of using these two medicines together in this patient group are being investigated.

This study plans to enroll 31 participants at Fudan University Shanghai Cancer Center in China. All participants will receive the same combination treatment. There is no comparison group, and both participants and study doctors will know which medicines are being given. Participants must be at least 18 years old, have at least one tumor that can be measured on a scan, and have adequate organ function and physical fitness for treatment. Doctors will review medical history, examine participants, and perform tests to check eligibility before treatment begins.

Participants will receive both medicines through an intravenous infusion once every three weeks. Pucotenlimab will be given at 200 mg, and becotatug vedotin at 2.0 mg per kilogram of body weight. Treatment may continue for up to two years but may stop earlier if the cancer worsens, side effects become unacceptable, a participant withdraws consent, or another reason specified in the study plan occurs. Study doctors may pause treatment, adjust the dose where appropriate, or stop treatment for safety reasons.

Participants will attend regular visits for examinations, blood and urine tests, heart checks, and monitoring of side effects. Tumor scans will be performed every two treatment cycles during the first six cycles and every three months afterward. A safety follow-up will take place about 30 days after the last dose, followed by survival follow-up approximately every 12 weeks.

The main outcome is the proportion of participants whose tumors shrink or disappear on scans. Researchers will also assess how long responses last, how long participants live without their cancer worsening, overall survival, and side effects. Possible risks include low blood cell counts, skin reactions, liver test abnormalities, nerve problems, and infusion reactions. Other serious or unexpected side effects may occur. Benefit is not guaranteed. Participation is voluntary, and participants may withdraw without affecting their usual medical care.
primary_outcomes: Objective Response Rate (ORR)
title: Becotatug Vedotin Plus Pucotenlimab for Metastatic Colorectal Cancer

brief_summary:
The research design adopts a sequential two-phase framework. The study will be conducted in three residential LTC facilities located in Taichung City or Changhua County, with a total planned enrollment of 60 residents. In Phase 1, 20 residents from one facility will participate in a six-week group music intervention, with one session per week. This phase will focus on multimodal image data construction and AI model development. Facial expression data will be manually annotated to establish reference standards for emotion recognition, while upper-limb movements will be analyzed using pose estimation and skeletal recognition techniques to extract dynamic features. These data will be used to develop and preliminarily validate an AI-based emotion and activity response monitoring model.

In Phase 2, 40 residents who did not participate in Phase 1 will be recruited and divided into four groups to participate in a six-week group music intervention, with one session per week. The AI model developed in Phase 1 will be implemented in the LTC setting to transform residents' facial emotional expressions and upper-limb activity responses into low-interference visual information for the music therapist as an adjunct to activity facilitation and professional judgment. Evaluation indicators include subjective psychosocial measures of loneliness, anxiety, and depression, with heart rate variability (HRV) assessed in Phase 2 as an objective physiological measure.

This study expects to establish a multimodal dataset and an AI-based emotion and activity response monitoring model for group music activities in LTC settings and to preliminarily evaluate the feasibility of a human-AI collaborative approach characterized by "AI-assisted monitoring and human professional decision-making.

title: Applying Comfort Theory to an AI-Assisted Group Music Intervention: Psychosocial and Physiological Outcomes and Feasibility in Long-Term Care Residents.

brief_summary:
Temporomandibular joint (TMJ) ankylosis is a condition in which the jaw joint becomes partially or completely fused, resulting in restricted mouth opening and difficulties with chewing, speaking, and daily activities. Surgical treatment aims to remove the ankylotic bone and restore normal jaw movement. Different bone-cutting devices can be used during surgery, but their effects on surgical efficiency, postoperative recovery, and quality of life may vary.

This prospective, non-randomized comparative clinical study aimed to compare three osteotomy techniques used in TMJ ankylosis surgery: piezoelectric surgery, an ultrasonic bone scalpel, and a conventional reciprocating saw.

A total of 32 patients undergoing TMJ ankylosis surgery were included. Eleven patients underwent surgery using a piezoelectric device, eleven using an ultrasonic bone scalpel, and ten using a conventional reciprocating saw. All surgical procedures were performed by the same surgeon under general anesthesia using a standardized surgical protocol.

The primary outcome was osteotomy time, measured during surgery. Secondary outcomes included total operative time, intraoperative blood loss, maximum mouth opening, postoperative pain, facial nerve function, and patient-reported quality of life. Facial nerve function was evaluated using the House-Brackmann grading system and the Sunnybrook Facial Grading System. Quality of life was assessed using the SF-12, WHOQOL-BREF, OHIP-14, and UW-QOL questionnaires.

Patients were followed for six months after surgery to evaluate functional recovery and changes in quality of life. The study aimed to determine whether the choice of osteotomy device was associated with differences in surgical efficiency, early postoperative recovery, and patient-reported outcomes.
primary_outcomes: Osteotomy Time
title: Comparison of Three Osteotomy Techniques in Temporomandibular Joint Ankylosis Surgery

brief_summary:
Graves' disease is an autoimmune condition that causes an overactive thyroid. Some people with Graves' disease develop thyroid eye disease, also called Graves' orbitopathy, which can cause swelling around the eyes, eye discomfort, double vision, changes in appearance, and, in severe cases, problems with vision.

The purpose of this study is to find out whether atorvastatin, a commonly used cholesterol-lowering medicine, can reduce the risk of developing active thyroid eye disease in adults who have recently been diagnosed with Graves' disease.

A total of 554 participants will be randomly assigned to one of two groups. One group will receive atorvastatin 40 mg once daily for 12 months in addition to standard treatment for Graves' disease. The other group will receive standard treatment for Graves' disease alone. Participants will be followed for 18 months.

During the study, participants will have regular assessments of their thyroid disease and their eyes. Blood samples and questionnaires about symptoms and quality of life will also be collected. The researchers will compare the two groups to determine whether atorvastatin reduces the development of active thyroid eye disease.
primary_outcomes: Development of Active Graves' Orbitopathy

brief_summary:
Nursing education requires innovative, student-centered teaching strategies that support the development of clinical competence, critical thinking, clinical decision-making, communication skills, and patient-centered care. Health assessment is a fundamental component of nursing curricula, enabling students to systematically collect and interpret patient data, distinguish normal from abnormal findings, and plan appropriate nursing care. However, clinical learning may be challenged by limited practice opportunities, high levels of student stress and anxiety, fear of making errors, and difficulties integrating theoretical knowledge with clinical practice. These challenges highlight the need for accessible and engaging educational approaches that strengthen students' professional development.

Game-based learning has emerged as a promising educational strategy for enhancing student motivation, active participation, knowledge acquisition, and clinical reasoning. In nursing education, it may also support the development of empathy, an essential component of patient-centered care. Empathy enables nursing students to understand patients' feelings, perspectives, and experiences and to incorporate this understanding into care delivery. Nevertheless, evidence regarding the combined effects of brief, practical game-based educational interventions on nursing students' care awareness and empathy remains limited.

This study aims to develop the "One Situation-Five Minutes" game and evaluate its effects on nursing students' care awareness and empathy using a mixed-methods research design. The intervention is designed as a brief, accessible, and student-centered learning activity that encourages students to consider clinical situations, recognize patients' needs, and reflect on the emotional and professional dimensions of nursing care. The educational approach is informed by Self-Determination Theory, which emphasizes the importance of autonomy, competence, and relatedness in promoting intrinsic motivation and meaningful learning.

The study will assess changes in nursing students' care awareness and empathy following participation in the game-based intervention. The qualitative component will explore students' experiences and perceptions of the intervention, providing further insight into its educational value and potential contributions to professional development. By integrating quantitative and qualitative findings, the study seeks to provide a comprehensive understanding of the intervention's effects and its applicability in nursing education.

The findings are expected to contribute to the evidence base for game-based learning in nursing education and inform the development of innovative teaching strategies that promote care awareness, empathy, and patient-centered nursing practice.
conditions: Nursing Students' Care Awareness and Empathy
primary_outcomes: Kiersma-Chen Empathy Scale Turkish Version (KCES-TR)
Interview Form
title: Development of the '1 Situation-5 Minutes' Game and Evaluation of Its Impact on Care Awareness and Empathy: A Mixed-Methods Study

This prospective observational cohort study aims to investigate the association between preoperative multimorbidity burden and functional recovery after primary total knee arthroplasty (TKA) in patients with knee osteoarthritis.

Approximately 230 adult patients undergoing elective unilateral primary TKA will be enrolled at a single hospital in Türkiye. Preoperative multimorbidity burden will be assessed using the Functional Comorbidity Index (FCI), which measures the presence of medical conditions that may affect physical function.

Patients will be evaluated before surgery and at 6 and 12 months after surgery. Functional outcomes and pain will be assessed using the Western Ontario and McMaster Universities Osteoarthritis Index (WOMAC) and Oxford Knee Score (OKS). Anxiety and depressive symptoms will be evaluated using the Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale (HADS).

The primary objective is to determine whether higher preoperative multimorbidity burden is associated with poorer physical function at 12 months after TKA. The study will also examine changes in functional recovery over time and other clinical outcomes.

All surgical procedures, postoperative care, and rehabilitation will follow routine clinical practice. No additional treatment or experimental intervention will be assigned as part of this study.

brief_summary:
A1 and A2 β-casein are genetic variants of β-casein in cow's milk that differ by a single amino acid at position 67. Digestion of A1 β-casein may result in greater release of beta-casomorphin-7 (BCM-7), an opioid peptide that may influence gastrointestinal function. Previous work from our group in lactose maldigesters found differences in gastric emptying following consumption of A1/A2 milk compared with A1 protein-free (A1PF) milk.

This randomized, masked, crossover study evaluated whether opioid receptor blockade with oral naloxone influenced gastric emptying following consumption of A1/A2 milk compared with A1PF milk in lactose maldigesters. Participants consumed each milk treatment with 2 mg oral naloxone during separate study visits. Gastric volume was measured using magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) over 120 minutes, and gastrointestinal symptoms were assessed. The study was designed to investigate whether opioid receptor signaling contributes to differences in gastric emptying between A1/A2 milk and A1PF milk.

brief_summary:
Acne is very common, especially among young adults. After acne heals, some people are left with persistent red or pink marks, called post-acne erythema (PAE). These marks can last for several months and, in some people, may be associated with a higher risk of developing acne scars.

PAE is more common in people with lighter skin. It is thought to happen because healing after acne can cause changes in the small blood vessels in the skin, making them wider and more visible. Skin irritation from some acne treatments may also contribute to the redness.

There is currently no single treatment that is considered the best treatment for post-acne redness. Several treatments have shown benefits, including different types of lasers and light treatments, as well as topical creams or serums such as vitamin C, tranexamic acid, oxymetazoline, and brimonidine. Timolol, a medication that can narrow small blood vessels, has also recently shown promising results.

Fractional CO₂ laser may help improve post-acne redness by stimulating skin healing and affecting the small blood vessels responsible for the redness. Other fractional lasers have also been shown to improve PAE.

Vitamin C is a powerful antioxidant that can help protect and repair the skin. When applied directly to the skin, it may reduce inflammation, support collagen production, and promote healing. Studies have shown improvement in post-acne redness with topical vitamin C.

Timolol is a medication that can cause narrowing of small blood vessels and may reduce the formation of new blood vessels. Because of these effects, it has recently been studied as a treatment for post-acne redness.

Because there is still no established standard treatment for PAE, this study was designed to compare three approaches: fractional CO₂ laser alone, fractional CO₂ laser combined with vitamin C, and fractional CO₂ laser combined with timolol. The goal is to determine which approach provides the best improvement in post-acne redness.
primary_outcomes: The percentage of improvement in post-acne erythema from baseline using erythema assessment scores.
title: Comparison of Fractional CO2 Laser Monotherapy and Its Combination With Either Topical Vitamin C or Topical Timolol in the Treatment of Post-Acne Erythema: A Split Face Study

brief_summary: This is a retrospective, single-center observational study evaluating the cognitive effects of hyperbaric oxygen therapy (HBOT) in adults who sustained a traumatic brain injury (TBI). Earlier randomized controlled work at this center demonstrated cognitive improvement after HBOT in patients with chronic deficits following mild TBI. This study evaluates a large sample size and operationalizes HBOT treatment as a continuous variable in the form of a cumulative oxygen dose, something has not been done before. Using the medical records of patients treated at the Sagol Center for Hyperbaric Medicine and Research at Shamir Medical Center between 2008 and 2026, the investigators compare computerized NeuroTrax cognitive assessments obtained before and after HBOT. The investigators quantify within-patient change across the cognitive domains and the Global Cognitive Score, and test whether the magnitude of cognitive change is associated with cumulative oxygen dose, expressed as the area under the pressure-time curve (ATA-minutes). The study includes patients across all TBI severity grades and adjusts for baseline performance, age, sex, and injury severity.

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn whether slowly dissolving stitches work as well as permanent stitches for repairing a groin (inguinal) hernia in adults using the Shouldice technique, a hernia repair that does not use mesh. Researchers think dissolving stitches may cause less long-term groin discomfort without making the hernia more likely to come back. The main questions it aims to answer are:

Is the chance of the hernia coming back within 1 year different with dissolving stitches (PDS) compared with permanent stitches (Prolene)?

Do the two types of stitches differ in complications, groin pain, quality of life, or the feeling of something foreign in the groin?

Is a larger future study of this question possible? This includes whether enough people join, whether the study plan is followed, and whether participants complete follow-up.

Researchers will compare slowly dissolving polydioxanone (PDS) stitches with permanent polypropylene (Prolene) stitches to see if the hernia comes back at similar rates and if patients have less long-term discomfort.

Participants will:

Have their planned open Shouldice hernia repair. The type of stitch will be chosen at random, like flipping a coin, during surgery.

Not be told which stitch they received until 1 year after surgery, or sooner if the hernia comes back or another operation is needed.

Complete questionnaires about pain, activity, and quality of life before surgery and about 30 days, 6 months, and 1 year after surgery.

See their surgeon for routine visits about 30 days and 1 year after surgery.

Receive one research phone call about 6 months after surgery.

Answer whether they feel something foreign in their groin and which type of stitch they think they received.
primary_outcomes: Number of Participants with Inguinal Hernia Recurrence
title: Permanent Versus Slowly Dissolving Stitches for Non-Mesh (Shouldice) Groin Hernia Repair

brief_summary: This study will compare the use of 27-inch and 55-inch endoscopic imaging monitors during minimally invasive surgery for women with endometrial cancer. Participants will be randomly assigned to one of the two monitor groups. All participants will undergo the same standard surgical procedure; only the monitor size used during surgery will differ. The main question is whether monitor size affects total operative time. The study will also evaluate sentinel lymph node dissection time, blood count changes, complications, infections, hospital stay, and drain-related outcomes during the first 30 days after surgery.

brief_summary: Periprosthetic joint infection (PJI) is a serious complication after joint replacement surgery and is difficult to treat. Poor nutritional status may impair the body's ability to recover and fight infection, as well as increase the risk of postoperative problems. The CONUT (Controlling Nutritional Status) score is a nutritional assessment tool that is based on 3 standard blood parameters, serum albumin, total cholesterol and total lymphocyte count. This study is a prospective observational study to investigate the association of preoperative nutritional status as defined by CONUT score and the risk of periprosthetic joint infection in patients undergoing joint arthroplasty. Preoperative nutritional assessment and postoperative follow-up will be performed to detect the occurrence of periprosthetic joint infection. We are studying whether a higher preoperative CONUT score is associated with a higher risk of infection after joint replacement surgery. The findings may help to identify those who are at increased risk of surgical infection and promote better preoperative assessment and patient care."
primary_outcomes: Incidence of periprosthetic joint infection
title: Impact of Nutritional Status Before Joint Replacement on Infection Risk

brief_summary:
Breast cancer is the most common cancer in women worldwide \[1\]. The burden is heaviest in low- and middle-income countries, where late detection, limited screening access and scarce biopsy resources delay diagnosis \[2,3\]. Accessible, non-invasive imaging that can triage patients accurately is therefore needed. Digital mammography and digital breast tomosynthesis are the reference tools for detecting microcalcifications, which are often the earliest visible sign of ductal carcinoma in situ (DCIS) and can appear before any mass or architectural distortion \[4\].

Microcalcifications also carry prognostic information that influences surgical planning and management \[5,6\]. They arise through comedonecrosis and through osteomimicry, in which tumor cells acquire bone-forming features \[6,7\]. Dynamic contrast-enhanced (DCE) breast MRI is highly sensitive for invasive cancer \[8\]. However, calcifications and metallic biopsy markers have very short T2 relaxation times and appear as signal voids that cannot be separated from air or fibrosis. Marker artifacts can measure 2-6 times the marker diameter and may obscure adjacent tumor \[9\]. Full lesion characterization may therefore need several examinations, radiation, contrast and biopsy.

Zero echo time (ZTE) MRI samples signal at an echo time of about 0 ms with a three-dimensional radial acquisition. With gray-scale inversion it gives CT-like contrast without radiation or contrast agent and is established in musculoskeletal imaging \[10\]. Whether ZTE adds value to routine breast MRI is unknown.

Research question: In women referred for diagnostic or staging breast MRI, does adding ZTE to the routine protocol accurately detect calcifications and improve biopsy-marker visualization compared with mammography and histopathology?
primary_outcomes: Diagnostic Accuracy, Marker Conspicuity, and Image Quality of ZTE Breast MRI
title: Diagnostic Accuracy and Utility of ZTE Added to Routine MRI

brief_summary:
This prospective randomized controlled clinical trial will compare the Buccal Periosteal Inversion Flap (BUPI) with the Buccal Advancement Flap (BAF) for the primary surgical closure of acute oro-antral communications (OAC) following tooth extraction in the posterior maxilla.

The primary objective is to determine whether the BUPI technique results in better preservation of keratinized gingival width compared with the BAF technique three months after surgery.

Secondary outcomes include successful closure rate of OACs, postoperative pain, swelling and bleeding, wound dehiscence or recurrence of the OAC, postoperative sinusitis or infection, reoperation rate, and operating time.

Participants will be randomly allocated in a 1:1 ratio to either BUPI or BAF. Clinical examinations and intraoral scans will be performed before surgery and at follow-up visits after 14 days, one month, and three months.
primary_outcomes: Change in Width of Keratinized Gingiva

brief_summary:
This study examined changes in substance use frequency, psychological well-being, and psychological symptoms among university students participating in a cognitive-behavioral therapy (CBT)-based group intervention.

A total of 90 university students participated in a three-group, non-randomized, quasi-experimental study. Participants were allocated according to their availability for scheduled sessions. The CBT group included 34 students who participated in seven weekly sessions lasting approximately 90 minutes each. The inactive control group included 33 students who received no intervention. The active comparison group included 23 students who participated in seven group counseling sessions focusing on personal development, communication, time management, motivation, and study skills.

Participants completed measures of substance use frequency, psychological well-being, and psychological symptoms before the intervention, after the intervention, and at a three-month follow-up.

The study aimed to compare changes in these outcomes across the three groups. Because group allocation was not randomized, the findings cannot establish that the intervention caused the observed changes.
primary_outcomes: Substance Use Frequency
title: Cognitive Behavioral Therapy for Substance Use and Mental Health in University Students

brief_summary:
During a subtalar fusion, the bones making up the subtalar joint (talus and calcaneus) are permanently fused together. In the procedure, any damaged cartilage and bone at the subtalar joint is removed, then screws are inserted into the joint to fuse the bones together. Depending on the surgeon, a bone graft is sometimes applied between the bones prior to screw insertion to aid in bone bridging (growth of bone into the fusion site). Participants who consent to this study and are assigned to the PliaFX® Flo Allograft group, will receive PliaFX® Flo Allograft (human tissue donated from a donor) at the fusion site. The PliaFX® Flo system is demineralized bone fibers (hard minerals removed from bone using acid) in a sterile syringe that allows for delivery into small areas where bone graft is needed to assist bone fusion. The allograft bone fibers are produced from donated human cadaver (deceased human) bone.

This study aims to determine whether the use of PliaFX® Flo Allograft in subtalar fusions will improve functioning and healing of the bone and cartilage for patients like you. Participants who are interested will discuss with their surgeon and be randomly assigned to one of the two study procedures below. The patient will not know what group they are in until after all data has been collected and all study visits are complete.
primary_outcomes: Bone Bridging Percentage
title: PliaFX Flo Subtalar Fusion Study

This project will aim to overcome this gap, showing for the first time in a DLB population, with a Randomized Controlled Trial (RCT), the feasibility and efficacy of a novel multimodal blue-enhanced Bright Light Treatment. Besides clinical outcomes, changes in melanopsin retinal ganglion cells (mRGCs) system will also be evaluated using a monochromatic light fMRI protocol. The results of this project will add valuable information to the current knowledge base of DLB for both scientific and clinical communities, helping clinicians in the prognosis and management of the disease, with the end goal of improving patients' quality of life.

brief_summary:
Dentists commonly use bitewing radiographs (dental X-rays) together with a visual-tactile (clinical) examination to detect cavities between the back teeth. While bitewing radiography can identify some lesions that are not visible during a visual-tactile examination, it is unclear whether its use improves outcomes that are important to patients. Radiographs may lead to the detection and treatment of lesions that would not otherwise cause problems, resulting in additional costs and dental procedures. Despite the widespread use of bitewing radiography in adult dental care, its effects on treatment decisions, patient outcomes, and cost-effectiveness have not been evaluated in randomized controlled trials among adults.

Therefore, the investigators aim to conduct a randomized controlled trial to compare two strategies for caries diagnosis in young adults: visual-tactile examination alone and visual-tactile examination supplemented with bitewing radiography. Participants will undergo a standardized oral examination and will be randomly assigned to one of the two diagnostic strategies. Treatment recommendations will be based on the findings obtained using the allocated diagnostic approach and will follow predefined treatment criteria.

The investigators will compare the effects of these diagnostic strategies on patient-important outcomes, treatment decisions, resource use, examination time, and cost-effectiveness. The results of this study will provide evidence on whether including bitewing radiography in routine caries diagnostics offers benefits that justify its additional costs and radiation exposure in young adults.

brief_summary:
Many women have an imbalance in their vaginal bacteria that can cause discomfort, irritation, and repeat infections. In a healthy vagina, helpful Lactobacillus bacteria are the main group of microbes. When they decline, other bacteria such as Gardnerella can take over. Most probiotic treatments for this problem are applied vaginally, and many women find them inconvenient. This study tested a probiotic capsule taken by mouth.

The capsule contained three Lactobacillus strains, taken from vaginal bacteria and from fermented foods. The study enrolled women aged 19 to 49 whose vaginal bacteria were in a borderline, mildly unbalanced state. Participants were randomly placed in one of three groups: a high-dose probiotic, a low-dose probiotic, or a placebo. They took their assigned product once a day for 12 weeks. Neither participants nor study staff knew who received which product.

The study looked at whether the probiotic improved the balance of vaginal bacteria, vaginal acidity, and symptoms, and whether it was safe to take.
primary_outcomes: Change in Nugent score
title: Oral Multi-Strain Lactobacillus Probiotic for Women With Vaginal Dysbiosis

brief_summary:
This multicenter, prospective, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial is designed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of early administration of Angong Niuhuang Pill in patients with disabling acute ischemic stroke.

Approximately 1,200 eligible participants will be randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to receive Angong Niuhuang Pill or a matching placebo for 5 consecutive days. Eligible participants will be adults aged 18 to 80 years with imaging-confirmed acute ischemic stroke involving the anterior circulation, a baseline National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS) score of 10 to 19, symptom onset or last known well within 24 hours before randomization, and a pre-stroke modified Rankin Scale (mRS) score of 0 or 1.

The primary efficacy outcome is the proportion of participants achieving functional independence at 90 days after randomization, defined as an mRS score of 0 to 2. Secondary outcomes include excellent functional outcome, the distribution of mRS scores at 90 days, change in the Barthel Index, changes in NIHSS scores, neurological improvement, and symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage. Safety outcomes include serious adverse events, all-cause mortality, and changes in hepatic and renal laboratory parameters.
primary_outcomes: Functional Independence at 90 Days
title: Early Administration of Angong Niuhuang Pill for Disabling Acute Ischemic Stroke (EAGER Trial)

brief_summary:
\### Study Summary - AcuteBike-ICU

Bed-cycling is commonly used as part of early rehabilitation in critically ill patients in the intensive care unit (ICU). However, the extent to which usual care bed-cycling activates the quadriceps muscles remains unclear, as does whether individualized exercise protocols can increase muscle stimulation.

The AcuteBike-ICU study is an experimental study aiming to compare the acute physiological responses to three bed-cycling protocols in critically ill patients: usual care constant work-rate cycling (u-CWR), individualized constant work-rate cycling (i-CWR), and individualized interval training (i-IT).

A total of 29 critically ill patients admitted to medical or surgical ICUs will be included. Participants will undergo an incremental loading test to determine their individual exercise capacity, followed by the different cycling protocols. The individualized continuous protocol involves cycling against a moderate resistance, whereas interval training alternates short periods of high-intensity cycling with passive cycling.

The primary outcome is quadriceps muscle activation, assessed using surface electromyography (sEMG) across four quadriceps muscle regions. Secondary outcomes include muscle fatigue, activation heterogeneity, muscle oxygenation and metabolism assessed using near-infrared spectroscopy (NIRS), as well as safety, feasibility, and patient-reported symptoms. Retrospective data from routine bed-cycling sessions will also be analyzed to characterize current clinical practice.

Each participant will complete the study within a maximum of five days.

By identifying which cycling protocol elicits the greatest quadriceps muscle stimulation, this study aims to support the development of more individualized and potentially more effective early rehabilitation strategies for critically ill patients.
interventions: usual care constant work rate bedcycling
primary_outcomes: Average Quadriceps Muscle Activation During Bed-Cycling
title: Quadriceps Muscle Activation and Oxygenation Responses During Usual Care Compared to Individualized Interval and Constant Work Rate Bed-cycling. An Experimental Study.

brief_summary:
Sexually transmitted infections (STIs) caused by Chlamydia trachomatis (CT) and Neisseria gonorrhoeae (NG) are increasing in France, with a significant proportion of asymptomatic infections. Standard management in sexual health clinics (called CeGIDD) relies on laboratory-based PCR tests with turnaround times of 24-72 hours, leading to frequent empirical antibiotic prescriptions, including broad-spectrum therapies. This practice contributes to antibiotic overuse and the emergence of antimicrobial resistance.

The OPTIMISE study evaluates the clinical impact of implementing the cobas® Liat® CT/NG point-of-care test (POCT) in CeGIDD settings. The hypothesis is that immediate, on-site molecular testing enables:

Significant reduction in unnecessary antibiotic prescriptions, particularly in asymptomatic exposed individuals, Targeted monotherapy in symptomatic patients, reducing broad-spectrum antibiotic exposure, Improved patient satisfaction and adherence through immediate diagnosis and treatment, Feasibility and acceptability of POCT integration in sexual health care pathways.

The study is a prospective, single-arm, bicentric interventional RIPH2 study including approximately 700 adults consulting in CeGIDD clinics of the Hospices Civils de Lyon, either for symptomatic STI suspicion or recent sexual exposure to CT/NG. Outcomes include the proportion of avoided antibiotic prescriptions, patient and provider satisfaction, and descriptive epidemiology of non-CT/NG pathogens.
primary_outcomes: Proportion of antibiotic prescriptions avoided using POCT cobas® Liat® CT/NG
title: Optimizing Antibiotic Prescription in STI Clinics Using Rapid POCT

brief_summary:
Background and Study Aims:

Melanoma is the most dangerous form of skin cancer, and early detection is crucial for improving patient outcomes. Over 90% of suspected skin cancer lesions are not melanoma, leading to a significant proportion of patients undergoing invasive skin biopsies for non-relevant lesions (1). Mitra Bio has developed a novel, non-invasive skin-tape test that captures skin cells from pigmented lesions that are suspected of being melanoma and detects the presence of melanoma-specific methylation biomarkers.

The goal of this study is to further develop and to prospectively clinically validate Mitra Bio's methylation biomarkers and algorithm, applied to skin samples collected non-invasively using skin-tapes, for the detection of melanoma.

Who can participate?

We will invite people from participating hospitals who:

-are scheduled for a standard of care biopsy of a suspicious lesion What does the study involve? All participants will have a one-time visit prior to their standard of care biopsy appointment. This visit will include clinical data collection, tape sample collection, and a participant survey.

Discovery Cohort: Involves using a tape sample collection method on the suspicious lesion, healthy contralateral skin, and the forehead.

Validation Cohort: Involves using tape sample collection method on only the suspicious lesion.

The participant's active role in the study concludes after this one visit. The research team will collect and review pathology data from the standard of care biopsy.

What are the risks and benefits of participating? This study could help improve non-invasive diagnostics for melanoma, significantly reducing the number of unnecessary biopsies. By taking part, you make that possible.

The tape sample collection is not painful and most people have no reaction. Mild and temporary skin redness and discomfort at the sampling site are the most common complaints.

Primary Validation Outcome
title: Development and Multi-Centre Validation of a Novel Non-Invasive Melanoma Molecular Diagnostic Test

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to compare three regional anesthesia techniques (spinal, epidural, and dural puncture epidural anesthesia) in healthy pregnant women undergoing planned (elective) cesarean delivery. The main questions it aims to answer are:

Which technique causes less low blood pressure (maternal hypotension) and requires less vasopressor medication during surgery? Which technique provides faster and more effective surgical anesthesia?

Spinal anesthesia works quickly but often causes a sudden drop in blood pressure, while epidural anesthesia is more stable but slower and sometimes incomplete. Dural puncture epidural is a newer technique that may combine the speed of spinal anesthesia with the stability of epidural anesthesia.

A total of 120 participants will be randomly assigned in equal numbers to one of the three groups. Researchers will compare the groups for blood pressure and heart rate changes, number of hypotension episodes, vasopressor use, time to reach adequate block (T6 level), block quality, need for additional pain medication, and side effects such as nausea, vomiting, and headache. Newborn well-being will be assessed with Apgar scores and umbilical cord blood gas analysis. Maternal and surgeon satisfaction will also be recorded.

primary_outcomes: Incidence of Maternal Hypotension
title: Comparing Spinal, Epidural, and Dural Puncture Epidural Anesthesia for Cesarean Delivery: Hemodynamics and Block Quality

brief_summary:
Reoperation is often required in surgical oncology because of positive resection margins and is associated with substantial physical, psychological, and economic consequences. Reoperation may also alter or delay the initiation of adjuvant therapy, potentially increasing the risk of local or distant recurrence. When re-resection is not feasible, a positive resection margin may necessitate additional treatment (e.g., radiation therapy or chemotherapy) that might otherwise have been avoided if clear margins had been achieved during the initial operation. Moreover, obtaining a negative margin during reoperation does not necessarily result in improved oncologic outcomes. Therefore, achieving negative margins intraoperatively is a key objective in oncologic surgery.

The AURA 10 Specimen PET/CT imaging system, a novel technology developed by a Belgian company, has recently been introduced to the market. This system enables perioperative imaging of resected tumors within approximately 10 minutes, allowing prompt assessment of surgical margins. Preliminary studies have demonstrated the potential clinical utility of this technique in various cancers, including breast, head and neck, and prostate cancers (1-5). A recent multicenter study of patients with breast cancer reported a sensitivity of 91% and a specificity of 86% for assessing surgical margin status in invasive ductal carcinoma (IDC) (4).

The aim of this study is to evaluate the clinical utility of perioperative specimen PET/CT imaging for surgical margin assessment and the feasibility of implementing this technology in routine clinical practice. The study will initially focus on breast cancer, head and neck cancer, soft tissue sarcomas, lung cancer, colorectal liver metastases, and hepatobiliary and pancreatic malignancies.

Patients will be screened for study eligibility. Those who meet the eligibility criteria will be invited to participate and provide written informed consent. On the day of the scheduled operation, patients will receive an injection of the FDG radiotracer in the Department of Nuclear Medicine approximately 1 hour before surgery. They will then be transfered by authorized personnel to the operating room. Immediately after tumor resection, the surgical specimen will be imaged using the specimen PET/CT imager (AURA 10, Xeos); this process will take approximately 10 minutes. If the surgeon decides to re-excise additional tissue, that tissue will also be imaged. In addition, all resected lymph nodes will be imaged for research purposes only.

The specimen will then be transferred to the histopathology laboratory for standard-of-care evaluation. During the operation, the results of specimen PET/CT imaging will not influence the surgeon's intraoperative decision-making. Subsequent clinical decisions will be based on the results of standard-of-care evaluations and the treating physician's clinical judgment. The final surgical margin status, as determined by the pathologist, will be collected for study purposes. Patients will receive treatment and follow-up in accordance with the standard of care, and relevant follow-up data will be collected.
lead_sponsor: Cliniques universitaires Saint-Luc- Université Catholique de Louvain
primary_outcomes: Sensitivity and specificity of perioperative specimen PET/CT (AURA 10, Xeos) for detecting tumor at the surgical margin on the resected mass.
title: Surgical Margin Assessment Using Intra-operative High-resolution PET/CT in Patients With Cancers Referred to Surgical Resection, an Exploratory Pilot Study

brief_summary: The purpose of this study is to evaluate the feasibility, acceptability, and preliminary effects of the Parent-Facilitated Early Oral-Sensory Experience (PEOE) program for very preterm infants in the Neonatal Intensive Care Unit (NICU). Very preterm infants (born before 32 weeks gestational age) often face challenges developing oral feeding skills. The PEOE intervention involves training parents to deliver gentle, synchronized oral-sensory stimulation-such as placing small droplets of human milk in the infant's mouth paired with gentle touch, voice, and scent-starting immediately before gavage feedings and potentially continuing into the feeding. This study uses a sequential two-group design. The first group of parents and infants will receive usual NICU care. The second group will receive the PEOE intervention. brief_summary:
Spinal Cord Injury (SCI) represents a significant health challenge, particularly when it comes to the ability to walk. Among its many consequences, mobility impairment can not only directly impact quality of life but also cause a series of secondary problems, such as urinary tract problems, breathing difficulties, muscle contractures, joint stiffness, and resulting pain. These effects can manifest early, even at a young age, further increasing the physical and psychological burden of those affected.

To address these challenges, the use of overground exoskeletons, such as the Ekso Bionics (USA), has attracted growing interest in both scientific research and clinical practice. The Ekso not only offers mobility but also represents a valuable resource for gait training, with potential direct and indirect benefits for the physical health and overall well-being of people with SCI. This study is a multicenter, retrospective, pre-post cohort study with the aim of evaluating the dose-dependent effects of exoskeleton-assisted walking training on level ground on spasticity and functional independence in individuals with spinal cord injury. The sample includes at least 70 participants with SCI underwed at least five sessions of walking training using the Ekso™ exoskeleton. Primary outcomes included changes in spasticity, measured by the aggregated Modified Ashworth Scale (MAS), and functional independence, assessed by the Spinal Cord Independence Measure (SCIM) III. The ultimate aim is therefore to evaluate whether ground-based exoskeleton-assisted gait training effectively reduces spasticity and improves functional independence in individuals with spinal cord injury, as this can support the integration of wearable motorized exoskeleons into standard spinal cord injury rehabilitation protocols.
conditions: Muscle Spasticity as a Result of Spinal Cord Injury
primary_outcomes: Modified Ashworth Scale (MAS)
title: Powered Exoskeleton-Assisted Walking in Persons With Spinal Cord Injury

brief_summary: This is an observational study that will follow adults with stage IV colorectal cancer whose disease has spread only to the liver (not to other organs) and who are undergoing a liver transplant as part of their cancer treatment. Liver transplantation is being offered as a potentially curative option for patients whose liver metastases cannot be surgically removed. Researchers will review participants' medical records for up to 5 years after transplant to understand how this treatment affects survival, cancer recurrence, and safety. Participants will also be asked to complete a quality-of-life questionnaire (EORTC QLQ-C30). Taking part in this study does not involve any additional tests, visits, or procedures beyond the standard care participants would otherwise receive.
primary_outcomes: Overall Survival (OS)
title: Liver Transplantation for Colorectal Cancer

brief_summary: The clinical study aims to evaluate the effect of iron supplementation in preventing the onset of Iron Deficiency Anemia during pregnancy. The trial is designed as a double-arm, double-blind clinical study comparing iron supplementation versus placebo in pregnant women. The primary objective is to assess the efficacy of iron supplementation in maintaining adequate levels of hemoglobin throughout gestation, while secondary outcomes include maternal hematological parameters and pregnancy outcomes.
primary_outcomes: Mean Hb levels
title: Safety and Efficacy of Iron Prophylaxis With on Iron Homeostasis in Healthy Pregnant Women

brief_summary:
The main purpose of this study is to look at how safe and well-tolerated LY4167586 is in participants with obesity or overweight with or without Type 2 Diabetes. Blood tests will be performed to check how much LY4167586 gets into the bloodstream and how long it takes the body to eliminate it following a single administration.

Participation in the study will last between approximately 53 to 89 weeks. For each participant (excluding those in Part B), the study will include between 5 and 7 stays in the Clinical Research Unit (CRU), each stay lasting between approximately 8 and 10 nights.
primary_outcomes: Number of Participants with One or More Serious Adverse Event(s) (SAEs) Considered by the Investigator to be Related to Study Drug Administration
title: A Study of LY4167586 in Participants With Obesity or Overweight With or Without Type 2 Diabetes

Eighty adults will be randomly assigned to four groups: immediate loading (within 48 hours) with a definitive zirconia crown, a permanent printed PMMA crown, or a temporary printed PMMA crown, or conventional loading with a definitive zirconia crown after 3 months. All implants are placed with a fully guided digital workflow.

brief_summary:
This Phase III randomized controlled trial will evaluate whether long-term use of the oral probiotic Streptococcus salivarius strain SALI-10 (SALI-10) can reduce the risk of radiation-related major adverse dental events (MADE) in patients with head and neck cancer receiving definitive or postoperative radiation therapy. MADE is defined as tooth failure and/or grade 2 or higher jaw osteoradionecrosis.

SALI-10 is a dual immunomodulatory and antimicrobial probiotic designed to colonize the oral cavity, promote a balanced oral microbiome, and help prevent the microbial dysbiosis and inflammation that commonly occur following radiation therapy. Participants will be randomly assigned to receive either standard of care alone or standard of care plus SALI-10 probiotic lozenges.

In addition to evaluating the effect of SALI-10 on dental and jaw complications, the study will assess changes in the oral microbiome and oral inflammatory load (OIL). Diagnostic imaging and dental imaging will also be analyzed to identify potential biomarkers associated with treatment response, toxicity, and the risk of radiation-induced dental complications. The hypothesis of this study is that the long-term use of SALI-10 for HNC patients receiving definitive or post-operative RT will decrease the risk of radiation-induced major adverse dental events.
primary_outcomes: Incidence of Major Adverse Dental Events (MADE)
title: SALI-10 Probiotic to Reduce Osteoradionecrosis and Dental Toxicity Following Radiation Therapy for Head and Neck Cancer

brief_summary:
Gingival inflammation is common and can often be reversed with effective daily oral hygiene. However, preventive care is not always delivered consistently in dental practices, and patients may not receive sufficient individualized training in oral self care and follow-up support.

This study will evaluate whether a structured preventive care workflow, called iMGi (individualized management of gingival inflammation), can be implemented consistently in routine dental practice.

Approximately 100 adults with plaque-related gingival inflammation will participate across multiple clinical centres. All participants will receive structured preventive care, including assessment of gingival health, individualized oral self-care training, professional preventive care, and follow-up appointments over approximately 10 months.

The main aim is to understand whether the workflow is practical for dental professionals to deliver, acceptable to patients and practitioners, and consistently applied across different clinical settings.

The researchers will also collect information on gingival bleeding, oral hygiene, patient experiences, and oral self-care behaviour to explore changes during the study.

The findings may help improve how preventive oral healthcare is organized and delivered in everyday dental practice.
primary_outcomes: Participant Completion of the iMGi Workflow
Adherence to Predefined iMGi Workflow Steps
title: Individualized Management of Plaque-Related Gingival Inflammation in Routine Dental Practice

brief_summary:
This prospective and retrospective, observational, monocentric study aims to investigate the longitudinal dynamics, phenotype, and functional properties of regulatory T cells (Tregs) in patients affected by hematological malignancies undergoing allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT) with post-transplant cyclophosphamide (PTCy)-based GvHD prophylaxis. Peripheral blood and bone marrow samples will be collected according to clinical practice at predefined timepoints and correlated with major transplant outcomes, including graft-versus-host disease (GvHD), relapse and graft-versus-tumor (GvT), infections, and inflammatory complications.

The study hypothesis is that quantitative and functional alterations of Tregs after HSCT influence immune tolerance, GvHD occurrence, and graft-versus-tumor activity, and that the characterization of Treg dysfunction may support the development of innovative CAR-Treg-based immunotherapeutic strategies to control GvHD and preserve GvT. This is a prospective and retrospective, observational, biological, monocenter study. The retrospective component will consist of a cohort of patients with previously biobanked biological samples, collected between 2013 and September 2026, which will serve as a control group for the laboratory analyses.
primary_outcomes: Treg functional activity in peripheral blood and bone marrow
Single-cell RNA sequencing profile of Treg cells
T-cell receptor (TCR) repertoire of Treg cells
Treg phenotype in peripheral blood and bone marrow
Incidence of acute and chronic GvHD
Major transplant outcomes
title: Unraveling Dynamics and Clinical Impact of Tregs in Allogeneic HSCT With PTCy

brief_summary:
When a tooth's nerve dies, inflammation can develop at the tip of the tooth's root. Root canal treatment is carried out to allow this inflammation to heal. Sometimes, inflammation persists in a tooth that has already undergone root canal treatment. In such cases, the root canals may be re-treated to allow the inflammation to heal.

During root canal treatment, the root canals inside the tooth are cleaned and then filled. Various instruments are used to clear the root canal along its entire length, so that the entire canal can be disinfected using antiseptic products. To allow these products to work more effectively, they can be activated. This activation can be achieved, amongst other methods, using vibrations caused by a plastic tip vibrating at a sonic frequency within the liquid. Another method of activation involves the use of a laser, which delivers pulsed energy. This creates shock waves in the liquid. Previous research has shown that root canals can be cleaned more effectively through the use of activation techniques.

This study aims to investigate whether the inflammation present at the root tip heals more effectively following the use of activation methods for the disinfectant. The use of the laser is compared with that of the sonic vibration instrument, and with a group in which the disinfectant is not activated. The effect of the activation method on post-treatment pain is also investigated.
primary_outcomes: post-operative pain
tooth survival
apical healing
title: Post-operative Pain and Apical Healing After Root Canal (re)Treatment With Laser-activated Irrigation Versus Sonic or no Activation

brief_summary: This is a single-arm, single-center exploratory study evaluating the safety and efficacy of gecacitinib administered in the peri-transplant period in patients with myeloid neoplasms and myelofibrosis (MF) who are scheduled to undergo allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (allo-HSCT).Approximately 10 eligible patients will receive oral gecacitinib starting 13 weeks before transplantation. Treatment will continue through the peri-transplant period and for up to 24 weeks after hematopoietic reconstitution. The primary endpoint is the engraftment rate at day +28 post-transplant. Secondary endpoints include poor graft function rate, grade III-IV acute GVHD rate, overall survival, infection rate, and bone marrow fibrosis grade changes.
primary_outcomes: Engraftment Rate at Day +28 Post-Transplant

brief_summary:
This phase II trial examine whether neoadjuvant PD-1 blockade will achieve a pathological response with manageable toxicity in stage IIB/IIC melanoma.

Patients with histologically confirmed AJCC (8th edition) clinical stage IIB (T3b, T4a), or IIC (T4b) primary cutaneous melanoma from a partial biopsy, with residual macroscopic disease without metastases will be included. They will be treated with 2 infusions of Pembrolizumab followed by surgery and adjuvant treatment.

The primary objective is to assess the pathological response of the primary tumor. Secondaries objectives include the evaluation of efficacy and safety as well as exploratory biomarkers analysis.
primary_outcomes: Major Pathological Response (MPR) according to central review
title: Neoadjuvant Pembrolizumab in Patients With High Risk, Stage IIB/IIC Cutaneous Melanoma: a Single Arm Proof of Concept Phase IIA Study.

brief_summary:
AI-CARE is an artificial intelligence-enabled clinical decision support mobile application designed to support prandial insulin dosing in individuals receiving MDI, incorporating a "human-in-the-loop" approach to ensure user verification of recommended doses. The application integrates AI-driven image-based carbohydrate estimation tailored to Asian dietary contexts, individualized patient-specific insulin parameters, and real-time CGM data to generate personalized insulin dose recommendations.

The primary objective of this study is to evaluate the feasibility, safety, and preliminary effectiveness of the AI-CARE mobile application among adults with diabetes receiving MDI. Feasibility will be assessed in terms of recruitment, retention, participant adherence, and application usability. Safety will be evaluated by monitoring the incidence of hypoglycaemia, hyperglycaemia, and other adverse events throughout the intervention period.

The study will also examine the preliminary effectiveness of AI-CARE on glycaemic and patient-reported outcomes compared with usual care. In addition, a qualitative process evaluation will be conducted to explore participants' experiences and perceptions of using AI-CARE, including perceived ease of use, usefulness, acceptability, and barriers and facilitators to real-world implementation. Findings from this phase will inform further refinement and optimization of the AI-CARE system and guide the design of a future large- scale randomized controlled trial.
primary_outcomes: Time to achieve target sample size
Eligibility rate
Recruitment rate
Retention and attrition rates
Intervention engagement
Intervention usability
title: AI-CARE: A Novel AI-Driven Mobile Insulin Calculator Integrating Image- Based Carbohydrate Estimation and CGM
