brief_summary:
This study investigates the effects of a tele-rehabilitation-guided Qigong exercise program on pulmonary function, functional exercise capacity, and symptom control in children and adolescents with mild-to-moderate asthma.

Participants aged 8 to 18 years will be randomly assigned to either an intervention group or a control group. The intervention group will participate in an 8-week, home-based, tele-rehabilitation-supervised Qigong exercise program in addition to standard medical care. The control group will continue receiving standard medical treatment and routine follow-up.

The primary aim of the study is to evaluate changes in pulmonary function (spirometric parameters such as FEV1 and FVC) and functional exercise capacity measured by the 6-Minute Walk Test (6MWT). Secondary outcomes include asthma symptom control assessed via the Asthma Control Test (ACT/c-ACT) and health-related quality of life.
primary_outcomes: Change from Baseline in Forced Expiratory Volume in 1 Second (FEV1)
Change from Baseline in 6-Minute Walk Distance (6MWD)
title: Effects of Tele-rehabilitation-Guided Qigong on Children and Adolescents With Asthma

brief_summary: Rural communities experience health care shortages of diabetes services provided by a registered dietitian nutritionist (RDN). This pilot study tested the feasibility of using rural community health screenings to recruit adults with Type 2 Diabetes (T2D) and provide Medical Nutrition Therapy (MNT), testing its impact on health, diet, and physical activity. Recruitment, retention, and adherence rates measured feasibility. Health markers (BMI, non-fasted blood glucose and lipids) were collected at an initial and follow up (6-9 months) screening. Diet (24-hr) and physical activity (7-day) recalls were collected at the MNT visits (initial, 1 mo, 3 mo). Paired t-tests and linear mixed models assessed mean differences between timepoints. Based upon the results from this pilot study, future testing of the efficacy of this approach in a randomized controlled study may be warranted and may allow for expansion of diabetes services in rural Indiana.
primary_outcomes: Feasibility outcome: Community health events
Feasibility outcome: Health screenings at community health events
Feasibility outcome: Recruitment Rate
Feasibility outcome: Retention rate
Feasibility outcome: Adherence rate
title: Effects of Adding a Registered Dietitian to Rural Community Healthy Behavior Support Services for Management of Type 2 Diabetes

brief_summary:
Background: Post-spinal hypotension occurs in 50-80% of cesarean deliveries and causes maternal nausea, vomiting, and reduced neonatal vigor; norepinephrine (NE), as boluses or prophylactic infusion, is the mainstay of treatment. Intermittent cuff monitoring cannot anticipate hypotension, whereas the Hypotension Prediction Index (HPI), derived from the noninvasive ClearSight arterial waveform, predicts hypotension (MAP \< 65 mmHg) up to 5 minutes in advance. A previous randomized trial by the investigators showed that HPI-guided management reduced hypotension burden and maternal nausea and vomiting during cesarean delivery. The investigators hypothesize that HPI-guided NE boluses provide better hypotension control than prophylactic NE infusion, with lower total NE dose, less reactive hypertension, and less maternal discomfort.

Methods: This single-center, randomized, open-label trial at National Taiwan University Hospital enrolls women aged 20-50 years with singleton pregnancies undergoing non-emergent cesarean delivery under neuraxial anesthesia. Exclusions: preeclampsia, NYHA class ≥ II cardiopulmonary disease, arrhythmia, pre-existing cardiovascular disease, BMI \> 40, and failed spinal or block below T6. A total of 180 parturients will be randomized 1:1:1 into three groups of 60 (51 per group required for 80% power, plus allowance for dropouts). All participants receive standard monitoring (ECG, pulse oximetry, cuff every 2.5 min, ClearSight, bilateral cerebral oximetry), a 1000 mL Ringer's preload, and combined spinal-epidural anesthesia with 12 mg of 0.5% hyperbaric bupivacaine. Hypotension is defined as MAP \< 65 mmHg and bradycardia as HR \< 60/min (treated with atropine 0.01 mg/kg). Group allocation is revealed to the anesthesiologist after block completion. The three groups differ in the monitoring used to guide treatment and in the mode of NE administration:

1. HPI bolus group (reactive boluses guided by continuous monitoring plus prediction): blood pressure is monitored with the ClearSight continuous arterial waveform and HPI, and no values are blinded. No prophylactic infusion is given. The target is HPI ≤ 85; when HPI exceeds 85 for 30 s, NE 5-10 mcg is given as a bolus (plus atropine 0.01 mg/kg if HR \< 60/min). If ClearSight MAP falls below 65 mmHg, NE 5-10 mcg is given immediately regardless of HPI.
2. ClearSight infusion group (prophylactic infusion guided by continuous monitoring): blood pressure is monitored with the ClearSight continuous arterial waveform; cuff readings and HPI are blinded. Prophylactic NE infusion begins immediately after spinal anesthesia at 0.04 mcg/kg/min and is titrated to maintain MAP ≥ 65 mmHg. Rescue boluses of NE 5 mcg (MAP 55-65 mmHg for 30 s) or 10 mcg (MAP \< 55 mmHg for 30 s) are given; the infusion is paused when MAP exceeds 100 mmHg for 30 s and resumed when MAP falls below 75 mmHg.
3. NIBP infusion group (control; prophylactic infusion guided by intermittent cuff monitoring): blood pressure is monitored with the conventional oscillometric cuff only; all ClearSight values are blinded. The same prophylactic NE infusion (0.04 mcg/kg/min, titrated to MAP ≥ 65 mmHg), rescue bolus thresholds (5 mcg for MAP 55-65 mmHg; 10 mcg for MAP \< 55 mmHg), and infusion-pause rule (MAP \> 100 mmHg, resume at \< 75 mmHg) are applied based on cuff readings.

The primary outcome is the time-weighted average of MAP \< 65 mmHg (TWA, mmHg) during the first 30 minutes after spinal anesthesia, calculated from ClearSight data in all groups. Secondary outcomes include umbilical arterial and venous blood gases (pH, pCO2, pO2, base excess, lactate); time-adjusted AUC for systolic pressure below 80% of baseline; incidence and total duration of hypotension; area under the 65 mmHg threshold; total NE and atropine doses; maternal symptoms (nausea, vomiting, bradycardia, dizziness, shivering); number of hypotensive events detected by cuff versus ClearSight; MAP and cerebral oximetry at eight time points (baseline through 15 min post-spinal); and breastfeeding effectiveness assessed with the LATCH score on postoperative day 2 and at discharge.

Statistical analysis: Continuous data will be compared by one-way ANOVA or Kruskal-Wallis test with Conover-Iman post hoc tests; categorical data by chi-square or Fisher's exact test; repeated measurements by repeated-measures ANOVA or linear mixed-effects models (two-tailed, p \< 0.05).

Safety and ethics: The intervention is low risk (finger-cuff discomfort, vasopressor-related hypertension or bradycardia, managed per protocol). Informed consent will be obtained and data coded and securely stored. Enrollment is planned from June 2026 to June 2028, with analysis and manuscript preparation through December 2028.
interventions: Hypotension Prediction Index derived from the noninvasive arterial waveform
Continuous noninvasive arterial pressure monitoring (HPI blinded)
intermittent oscillometric blood pressure monitoring (standard care)
primary_outcomes: Time-weighted average of hypotension (TWA MAP < 65 mmHg)
title: Comparison of HPI-guided Norepinephrine Boluses, ClearSight-guided Norepinephrine Infusion, and Oscillometric-guided Norepinephrine Infusion for Blood Pressure Stability During Cesarean Delivery

brief_summary: This is a prospective-retrospective, translational, no profit, multicentric, observational study. A cohort of at least 100 early-onset JIA patients attending the Unit of Rheumatology and Autoinflammatory Diseases, Department of Pediatric Sciences, IRCCS Istituto Giannina Gaslini or selected Italian pediatric rheumatology centers, will be enrolled and evaluated at onset and at 5 time points of follow up to 24 months (month 3, month 6, month 12, month 18 and month 24) to monitor the course of the disease. A cohort of 30 patients with Iridocyclitis not correlated to JIA will be recruited in parallel at the time of disease diagnosis as a group of control for comparison.
primary_outcomes: Construction of an integrated multiparametric prediction model
title: Development of a Multidimensional Prediction Model for the Course and Outcome of Early-Onset Juvenile Idiopathic Arthritis (JIA)

brief_summary: STEREOPANC is a randomized, controlled, open label, multicenter study initiated by the Oulu HPB Study Group. Patients with a very high risk of B/C POPF (soft pancreas) scheduled for PD for any indication are recognized at a local HPB MDT. Patients are randomized to either intervention arm (preoperative SBRT in 3 x 6,6Gy fractions = 19.8 Gy) or control arm (conventional treatment) with a ratio of 1:1. Participating centers are Oulu University Hospital, Kuopio University Hospital and Central Hospital of Northern Carelia, Finland.
primary_outcomes: Rate of postoperative grade B/C pancreatic fistulae
title: Stereotactic Body Radiotherapy (SBRT) Induced Pancreatic Atrophy for Prevention of Post Operative Pancreatic Fistulae (POPF) After Pancreatoduodenectomy in Very High-Risk Patients (STEREOPANC)

brief_summary:
The goal of this open-label, single-arm, multicenter study is to assess the efficacy and safety of Batten-1 (oral liquid formulation of miglustat) (15 mg/kg up to 600 mg/day) in approximately 27 pediatric subjects with CLN3 disease over a period of 52 weeks, using visual acuity as primary efficacy endpoint, The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Does Batten-1 slow down or stabilize the visual acuity decline in pediatric CLN3 patients ?
* What medical problems do participants have when taking Batten-1? in comparison with an external group of non-treated CLN3 disease subjects from natural history studies.

After a titration period of 8 weeks, participants will take Batten-1 every day up to 52 weeks and will visit the clinic every 24 weeks for checkups and tests.

Participants will keep a diary for potential seizure occurrence and compliance to study drug. Interventions they'll be given include:

* visual acuity assessement
* motor and capability assessement
* safety assessment including lab tests and electrocardiogram
* assessment of the effect of the body on Batten-1
* assessment of quality of life
primary_outcomes: Best Corrected Visual Acuity (BCVA)
title: Study With Batten-1 (Miglustat Liquid Formulation) to Treat Ceroid Lipofuscinosis Neuronal 3 (CLN3) Disease

brief_summary: The objective of this study is to assess vaccination coverage (VC) for vaccines recommended during pregnancy (pertussis, COVID-19, seasonal influenza, and respiratory syncytial virus \[RSV\] infection), their acceptability, and the factors associated with this acceptability among pregnant women and healthcare professionals in several maternity units in the Île-de-France region. We plan to estimate vaccination coverage using health-related (type of follow-up) and relevant socio-educational strata at the regional level in Île-de-France. An overall estimate of vaccination coverage for the Île-de-France region will be obtained by weighting according to regional data for these strata. Estimates of vaccination coverage according to determinants-particularly socio-educational factors-will allow extrapolation to other French regions, in order to better define strategies for promoting vaccination among pregnant women and the healthcare professionals who care for them. The wide diversity of maternity unit profiles in Île-de-France, together with the substantial socio-educational diversity of the regional population, will enable a nuanced and comprehensive overview.
primary_outcomes: Survey to Estimate Vaccination Coverage Against Pertussis, COVID-19, Seasonal Influenza, and RSV Infection Among Pregnant Women in Maternity Units in the Île-de-France Region.
title: Assessment of the Acceptability of, and Factors Associated With, Recommended Vaccinations During Pregnancy in Maternity Units in the Ile-de-France Region

brief_summary:
The goal of this quasi-experimental study is to evaluate the effect of range of motion (ROM) exercises on pain and functional ability among adult patients of both genders with second-degree burn injuries affecting the upper and/or lower extremities.

The main questions addressed by the study are:

Do range of motion exercises reduce pain levels among patients with second-degree burn injuries? Do range of motion exercises improve the functional ability of burned upper and/or lower extremities among patients with second-degree burn injuries?

A comparison between the study group receiving range of motion exercises and the control group receiving routine care will be conducted to evaluate the effects of range of motion exercises on pain levels and functional ability.

Study participants will undergo the following procedures:

Assessment of pain levels before implementing range of motion exercises. Assessment of the functional ability of burned upper and/or lower extremities before implementing range of motion exercises.

Implementation of range of motion exercises for the study group according to the study protocol.

Provision of routine care to the control group. Post-intervention assessment of pain levels and functional ability to evaluate changes following the intervention.
conditions: Impact of ROM Exercises on Pain and Functional Ability in Patients With Second -Degree Burns
primary_outcomes: Patient's Structured Interview Questionnaire
Change in Pain Intensity
Change in Functional Ability of the Affected upper Extremities
Change in Functional Ability of the Affected lower Extremities
title: Impact of Range of Motion Exercises on Pain and Functional Ability

brief_summary:
This single-center, non-controlled, single-arm clinical study is designed to evaluate the performance and safety of the Class III investigational device MD60002 (composed of highly purified polynucleotides at 3%) for aesthetic use in the treatment of skin imperfections and wrinkles caused by physiological facial aging.

A total of 43 adult subjects presenting with facial wrinkles (Lemperle Wrinkle Severity Scale score ≥ 1) will be enrolled. Participants will receive intradermal injections of MD60002 according to a standardized protocol.

The primary endpoint is the evaluation of aesthetic improvement measured by the change in the Lemperle Wrinkle Severity Scale (LWSS) score from baseline to the 30-day follow-up visit. Secondary endpoints include patient-reported subjective satisfaction evaluated via the Global Aesthetic Improvement Scale (GAIS), alongside comprehensive safety, tolerability, and device deficiency monitoring in accordance with ISO 14155 guidelines.
primary_outcomes: Change from Baseline in Lemperle Wrinkle Assessment Scale (LWSS) Score
Incidence and Severity of Treatment-Emergent Adverse Events (TEAEs) and Device Defect Logs
Investigator Global Aesthetic Improvement Scale (GAIS) Rating
title: Evaluation of MD60002 Device for Facial Skin Aging

brief_summary:
The goal of this feasibility study is to evaluate the study protocols of a future larger clinical study.

In this study children, aged 3-7 years, with caries lesions in their primary molars will be treated with stainless steel crowns or conventional fillings. Treatment results will be compared and participating children, parents and dentist will be asked questions about the treatments and the study protocol. The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Children, parents and dentists´ acceptance of study protocols
* Practical/logistical issues for the public dental clinics during the study
* Find out if there is a difference in treatment result between stainless steel crowns and conventional fillings Researchers will compare treatment with stainless steel crowns to conventional fillings to see if there are any difference in treatment results and how children and parents view the treatment.

Participants will receive dental treatment and follow up controls at their public dental clinic. Children, parents and participating dentist will be asked to fill out surveys before, during and after treatment and follow up controls
primary_outcomes: Parents and dentists' acceptance of study protocols assessed qualitatively in semi-structured interviews.
Time for recruitment of participants to the study
Drop-out rate
title: This Feasibility Study Will Evaluate the Study Protocols for Treatment and Follow-up Controls of Primary Molars With Caries in Children Treated With Stainless Steel Crowns or Conventional Fillings. Treatment Success and Potential Failures Will be Followed at 3, 6 and 12 Months Post Treatment.

brief_summary: Current advance care planning (ACP) tabletop games mostly focus on exploring "personal values." While a few explore care preferences through "hypothetical scenarios," they are not disease-oriented, which can create discrepancies between the scenarios or medical treatments and the patient's actual condition and may fail to capture the patient's true preferences. A systematic review found that disease-oriented ACP interventions effectively capture patients' and their families' preferences for medical treatments because they closely reflect the patient's actual disease progression. However, no disease-oriented scenario games are currently available. Therefore, this study, using heart failure as an example, aims to develop and evaluate the impact of disease-oriented scenario games on older adults and family caregivers in ACP.
primary_outcomes: The Questionnaire on Life Support Preferences for Heart Failure Patients (QLSP-HF)
title: Development and Evaluation of a Disease-oriented Scenario Game to Promote ACP Among Older Adults and Family Caregivers

brief_summary: This observational study aims to investigate the clinical significance of internal carotid artery dolichoarteriopathy, including tortuosity, kinking, and coiling, and to identify factors associated with cerebral dysfunction and adverse cerebrovascular outcomes. The study combines retrospective clinical data with prospective follow-up of patients with verified internal carotid artery dolichoarteriopathy. Anatomical, hemodynamic, neuroimaging, clinical, cognitive, and biomarker characteristics will be evaluated to develop and validate a multimodal approach to risk stratification. Outcomes will also be compared between patients managed surgically and conservatively according to routine clinical indications. Treatment decisions are made independently by the treating physicians and are not assigned by the study protocol.
primary_outcomes: Incidence of Ipsilateral Ischemic Stroke and/or Transient Ischemic Attack
title: Clinical Significance of Internal Carotid Artery Dolichoarteriopathy

brief_summary:
The goal of this observational study is to learn how patients' vital signs and symptoms change during outpatient CAR T-cell therapy with lisocabtagene maraleucel (liso-cel), a type of cancer treatment. The study tracks vital signs and other health data at home using wearable monitoring devices. It includes adults with blood cancers who are receiving liso-cel as outpatients, meaning they are at home rather than staying in the hospital during treatment.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

* What do patients' vital signs and monitoring data look like from 3 days before through 14 days after their CAR T-cell infusion, and what side effects do they experience, such as cytokine release syndrome (a fever and inflammation reaction) and neurological side effects?
* How are patients' individual characteristics and monitoring data related to these side effects?

Participants will:

* Use the Current Health home monitoring kit, including a wearable device that tracks breathing rate, pulse, oxygen levels, skin temperature, and step count, plus a blood pressure cuff, a temperature patch, a thermometer, a tablet, and a device that sends data without needing home internet. Monitoring starts 3 days before infusion and continues for 14 days afterward, pausing during any hospital stays.
* Answer short questions about their experience on the tablet.
* Continue their regular medical care and appointments. The study team will collect information from their medical records, such as test results, treatment details, and any side effects or complications.

Participants receive CAR T-cell therapy as part of their regular care. The study does not test or change any treatment. Researchers are only observing and recording what happens during this at-home care model.

brief_summary:
Gingivitis is an early and reversible form of periodontal disease characterized by an increased inflammatory response to dental biofilm. As gingivitis progresses, increased production of reactive oxygen species as part of the host response contributes to oxidative stress, leading to structural damage to DNA, proteins, and lipids in both local and systemic biological environments. One of the major indicators of this oxidative process is 8-hydroxy-2'-deoxyguanosine (8-OHdG), a critical biomarker reflecting the biochemical severity of periodontal inflammation. In addition, malondialdehyde (MDA), an end product of lipid peroxidation, reflects the level of oxidative stress, whereas total antioxidant capacity (TAC) serves as a complementary biochemical marker for assessing the antioxidant defense response of the host. Furthermore, C-reactive protein (CRP), a marker of systemic inflammation, may provide valuable information regarding the effects of gingival inflammation on the host.

Non-surgical periodontal treatment (NSPT) is the standard treatment approach for gingivitis; however, oxidative stress may not be completely suppressed following treatment, and persistent alterations in certain biomarkers may remain. Alpha-lipoic acid (ALA) is a potent antioxidant capable of neutralizing reactive oxygen species, supporting endogenous antioxidant systems, and exerting antioxidant activity in both lipid- and aqueous-phase environments. However, no clinical study has evaluated the effects of systemic ALA supplementation as an adjunct to NSPT on 8-OHdG, MDA, TAC, and CRP levels in individuals with gingivitis.

Therefore, this study aims to analyze 8-OHdG, MDA, TAC, and CRP levels in saliva and serum samples from periodontally healthy individuals and individuals with gingivitis and to determine the effects of adjunctive ALA supplementation to NSPT on biomarkers of oxidative stress and inflammation. This approach is expected to provide novel evidence regarding the potential biochemical benefits of antioxidant supplementation in the management of gingivitis.
primary_outcomes: Salivary 8-OHdG
title: Alpha-Lipoic Acid as an Adjunct to Non-Surgical Periodontal Treatment in Gingivitis

brief_summary:

Flexible flatfoot is common in children and can affect how weight is distributed on the foot, balance, and athletic abilities. While both foot-strengthening exercises and jump training (plyometrics) are helpful, it is not known which one should be done first to get the best results.

In this study, thirty-six young male football players with flexible flatfoot were divided into three groups. The first group performed jump training followed by foot muscle strengthening. The second group did the foot muscle strengthening first, followed by jump training. The third group served as a control group and did not change their usual training. The researchers measured changes in foot pressure, balance, jumping height, muscle force, and sprint speed before and after the training to find out which exercise order is most effective for improving athletic performance and foot loading.

brief_summary:
Intensive care units (ICUs) are high-technology, high-performance units where patients with life-threatening conditions receive advanced nursing care and continuous monitoring. Pediatric intensive care units (PICUs), a specialized area within ICUs, provide closer observation and treatment than general wards and deliver services in a separate unit.

Among the treatments frequently used during PICU stays, children most often receive mechanical ventilation (MV), endotracheal tube, or tracheostomy support because of respiratory diseases and respiratory failure. Endotracheal intubation is the most common means of securing the airway. It is indispensable for airway control in PICUs and is of primary importance for ensuring optimal ventilation and oxygenation. Children receiving MV are exposed to painful stimuli an average of 10-14 times per day, and endotracheal suctioning is one of the most painful procedures for these children. Tracheostomy is a surgical method used to maintain airway patency. Tracheostomy suctioning is part of routine care aimed at preventing infection and obstruction, while also maintaining airway patency.

Suctioning is an important nursing intervention in PICU patients with an endotracheal tube or tracheostomy to maintain airway patency and prevent potential infections. Following routine invasive procedures that cause pain, such as suctioning, adverse physiological, metabolic, and behavioral responses may develop in children as stress and the duration and intensity of pain increase. The literature indicates that suctioning causes physiological changes such as pain, restlessness, tachycardia, hypertension, and decreased oxygen saturation, and that these effects are more pronounced in pediatric patients. This necessitates a holistic approach to health that links pain not only to physical conditions but also to psychological and emotional processes. However, the limited doses in which pharmacological analgesics can be used in pediatric patients, the risk of side effects, and the fact that sedation before a procedure is not always possible increase the importance of alternative pain management methods. In this context, nonpharmacological interventions such as listening to classical music can be used both to reduce the pain children experience during procedures and to regulate physiological stress responses.

Studies have shown that pain perception decreases, heart rate and respiratory rate are regulated, and anxiety is markedly reduced in children who listen to classical music. The effect of music is based on the stimulation of emotional centers through the limbic system and, through this pathway, the balancing of physiological parameters such as heart rate, blood pressure, and respiration via the autonomic nervous system.

Accordingly, this study aims to comparatively examine the effects of classical music played during two different suctioning methods (endotracheal and tracheostomy suctioning) on pain levels and physiological parameters in children receiving care in a pediatric intensive care unit. The limited number of studies on classical music applied during specific, brief invasive procedures such as suctioning underscores the originality of this study and increases its potential to contribute to evidence-based practice in pediatric nursing.

Physiological Parameters Form
title: Classical Music, Pain, and Physiological Parameters in Children Undergoing Two Aspiration Procedures

brief_summary:
Following a tooth extraction, the loss of alveolar bone is inevitable. As the site remodels, the alveolar ridge naturally shrinks in both height and width (Schropp et al., 2003). This loss of bone volume can make dental implant placement challenging, frequently requiring bone grafting procedures to rebuild the necessary foundation for the implant.Guided bone regeneration (GBR) stands as a leading strategy for repairing osseous defects. When employing particulate bone grafts, this approach typically depends on the application of barrier membranes to promote the regeneration of bone tissue (Retzepi \& Donos, 2010).Various regenerative approaches have been proposed to restore ridge width: among these, guided bone regeneration (GBR) using a combination of autogenous bone and xenogenic grafts has gained widespread acceptance due to its biological properties and ability to achieve stable dimensional augmentation (Urban et al., 2013).Historically, various methods have been implemented to enhance both the volume and structural integrity of newly formed bone. An ideal graft material must act as an effective osteoconductive scaffold, facilitating cellular ingrowth while preserving its dimensional stability. Although autogenous bone is still considered the gold standard for these procedures, it is prone to significant volumetric resorption as time progresses (Gulinelli et al., 2017).To counteract volume loss during the remodeling process, researchers have proposed combining autogenous bone with allogenic, xenogenic, or alloplastic substitutes (Chappuis et al., 2017). This composite grafting strategy is designed to enhance both the structural stability and overall quality of the augmented site, while simultaneously decreasing surgical morbidity by minimizing the volume of autogenous bone required for harvest (Mendoza-Azpur et al., 2019).

Even though composite grafts are routinely employed in clinical practice, the ideal proportion of autogenous bone to xenogenic material in guided bone regeneration (GBR) protocols has yet to be definitively established.
primary_outcomes: Radiographic Horizontal Bone Gain
title: Autogenous and Xenograft Bone Mix in Alveolar Ridge Reconstruction

If the initial shock does not restore normal heart rhythm, further shocks will be delivered according to the study protocol.

The study will compare the proportion of participants in each group whose normal heart rhythm is restored shortly after cardioversion and whose rhythm remains stable. The study team will also record complications, changes in selected laboratory measures and quality of life, medication use, and treatment costs.

brief_summary:
Throughout the diagnostic and treatment process, pediatric patients are subjected to invasive procedures-such as peripheral intravenous catheterization (PIVC)-that cause pain, stress, fear, and anxiety. PIVC is one of the most commonly used procedures in modern medicine. This method is used for a variety of procedures, including intravenous fluid support, continued medication administration, monitoring of hemodynamic parameters, and the provision of total parenteral nutrition. However, the narrow diameter of veins in children and the fact that their vascular structure is not yet fully developed make the PIVC procedure more challenging compared to adults and often result in unsuccessful attempts. Particularly in time-critical units such as the emergency department, multiple failed attempts can lead to prolonged procedure times and various complications.

Inadequate vascular access can lead to negative emotional reactions in children-such as pain, fear, and anxiety-as well as disruptions in the treatment process, tissue damage, an increased need for diagnosis and treatment, an increased workload for healthcare providers, and higher healthcare costs. Furthermore, repeat procedures lead to increased parental anxiety and a decline in trust in healthcare services. Therefore, when approaching children within the framework of the principle of atraumatic care, the goal should not be the complete elimination of pain, but rather the reduction of the duration and intensity of exposure to it.

In this context, the proposed study aims to conduct a comparative analysis of the effects of distractions and technological interventions used during invasive procedures on children and their parents. By integrating these methods-which have been evaluated in only a limited number of studies in the literature-into nursing care, the study aims to develop evidence-based recommendations for improving patient comfort and reducing traumatic experiences.

Research Hypotheses

H0: There is no difference between the groups in terms of pain, fear, anxiety, procedure duration, and anxiety scores associated with central venous catheterization.

H1a: There is a difference between the groups in pain scores in children associated with the PIVC procedure.

H1b: There is a difference between the groups in fear scores in children associated with the PIVC procedure.

H1c: There is a difference between the groups in terms of anxiety scores in children associated with the PIVC procedure.

H1d: There is a difference between the groups in terms of worry scores in parents associated with the PIVC procedure.

H1e: There is a difference between the groups in terms of procedure durations associated with the PIVC procedure.

Data Collection Tools The study will use the Demographic Information Form, the Wong-Baker Facial Expression Rating Scale, the Children's Fear and Anxiety Scale, and the State-Trait Anxiety Inventory (STAI) to measure parental anxiety, and data will be collected while taking the duration of the procedure into account.

title: Effect of Buzzy and Virtual Reality on Children Undergoing Venous Procedures

* Control group: receives standard dietary counseling alone.

The total study participation for each patient is 60 days, during which changes in muscle mass, muscle quality, physical function, quality of life, and blood and stool biomarkers will be evaluated.

brief_summary:
Spinal anaesthesia is the preferred technique for elective caesarean section, but it is frequently complicated by maternal hypotension and bradycardia. Activation of serotonin (5-HT3) receptors in the cardiac vagal afferents has been proposed as one mechanism of the Bezold-Jarisch reflex, which may contribute to sudden bradycardia and vasodilation after spinal anaesthesia. Ondansetron is a selective 5-HT3 receptor antagonist.

This randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial evaluated whether a single intravenous dose of ondansetron 4 mg given 5 minutes before spinal anaesthesia reduces maternal hypotension, bradycardia and the need for rescue medications (ephedrine and atropine) in women undergoing elective caesarean section. Haemodynamic variables and pulse oximetry-derived perfusion index (PI) and pleth variability index (PVI) were recorded at predefined time points, including during a passive leg raising manoeuvre before spinal anaesthesia.

primary_outcomes: Incidence of maternal hypotension

brief_summary: Dissociated vertical deviation (DVD) is a slow, disconjugate upward drift of the non-fixating eye, usually with abduction and excyclotorsion, that does not obey Hering's law . It is uncommon in the general population but develops in about half to 90% of children with infantile esotropia . Its cause is uncertain, probably a supranuclear vertical vergence disturbance after early disruption of binocular fusion, which explains its association with infantile esotropia . Non-surgical treatment suits small or well-controlled deviations: refractive correction, amblyopia therapy . Surgery is indicated when the deviation is frequently manifest or cosmetically unacceptable . When inferior oblique overaction coexists, anterior transposition of the inferior oblique is the procedure of choice . In isolated DVD, surgery aims mainly to weaken the superior rectus (SR). Conventional graded SR recession is the most widely used , but large deviations may need 10 mm or more and undercorrection is common . Recession-resection resects part of the muscle then recesses it by a greater amount, raising the weakening effect , while fenestration removes a central block of muscle and tendon near the insertion without sutures and is simpler and faster . Other options are a posterior fixation (Faden) suture and Y-splitting . The evidence is weak: a Cochrane review found the published studies small and retrospective and asked for randomized trials , and the only comparison of three SR techniques allocated patients by deviation size rather than at random . No trial has compared fenestration with recession-resection in children with DVD.
primary_outcomes: Compare success rates in the 3 groups.
title: Comparative Study Of Combined Recession-Resection And Fenestration of Superior Rectus Muscle for Treatment of Dissociated Vertical Deviation

brief_summary:
This study will test whether taking ginger supplements can increase ghrelin, a hunger hormone that is decreased in the blood of people with Parkinson's disease (PD) and REM Sleep Behaviour disorder (RBD). Three groups of participants are taking part:

1. People with Parkinson's disease (PD);
2. People with REM Sleep Behaviour Disorder (RBD);
3. Healthy people of similar age and sex.

The investigators aim to include 24 participants per group. Each participant will take ginger capsules for 12 weeks at one of two dose levels (0.24g or 0.48g of ginger root extract supplement) allocated at random.

The main goal is to find out whether ginger causes a dose-related increase in blood ghrelin levels.

Secondary goals are to explore whether ginger:

1. reduces levels of inflammation in the blood
2. improves gut symptoms including constipation
3. is well tolerabled in people with Parkinons's

If the study shows that ginger increases ghrelin levels, it will provide important early evidence to support a future larger clinical trial to determine whether ginger supplements could help slow or modify Parkinson's disease by increasing blood ghrelin levels.

primary_outcomes: Change in fasting blood acylated and unacylated ghrelin levels in PD, RBD and controls over 12 weeks of ginger supplementation.

* Wear a sensor for 13 weeks to measure their sleep and light exposure.

brief_summary:
Memory and thinking problems in older adults, including mild cognitive impairment (MCI) and Alzheimer's disease (AD), can be difficult to assess promptly because evaluation often depends on in-person specialist visits. MonitorCog-AI is a computer-based platform designed to provide a more accessible way to assess and monitor cognitive changes using standard computers or tablets. Artificial intelligence (AI) will be used to analyze the digital information collected by the platform and examine whether combining several types of measures improves assessment of cognitive impairment.

The study will include 60 adults aged 50 years and older: 20 healthy adults, 20 adults with MCI, and 20 adults with AD. Participants will be assessed at baseline, 6 months, and 12 months. At each timepoint, participants will complete one clinical assessment and one digital assessment. The clinical assessment will include standard measures of memory and thinking, an assessment of daily functioning, and a brief recording of brain electrical activity. The digital assessment will take approximately 60-80 minutes and will assess five areas: cognition, eye movements measured using a webcam, language, speech, and fine-motor performance measured using a mouse. At baseline, the digital assessment will be completed in the clinic; at 6 and 12 months, it will usually be completed remotely at home.

The study has three main goals. First, it will determine whether MonitorCog-AI is feasible, acceptable, easy to use, and not overly burdensome for repeated assessment. Second, it will examine how well AI-based analysis of the digital measures distinguishes healthy adults, adults with MCI, and adults with AD, and whether combining several types of digital information performs better than any single type alone. Third, it will examine how digital measures change over 12 months and whether these changes are related to changes in clinical measures of cognition and daily functioning.
lead_sponsor: Centre for Addiction and Mental Health
primary_outcomes: Participant Completion Rate
System Usability Scale (SUS) Score
Participant Acceptability of MonitorCog-AI
User Burden Scale (UBS) Score
title: Remote Digital Assessments for Cognitive Disorders

After providing written informed consent, participants will undergo screening to determine whether they are eligible. Eligible participants will be randomly assigned to a study group and receive a single dose of the investigational product on Day 0.

Participants will record solicited adverse events in a subject diary from Day 0 through Day 7. brief_summary: The purpose of this study is to learn how the sweet taste and the calorie content of a beverage affect the way people respond to the brand logo printed on that beverage. Previous work suggests that once a logo has been paired repeatedly with a rewarding drink, the logo alone can capture attention and increase the desire to consume. What is not yet known is whether the sweet taste, the calories, or both are responsible. Two current scientific explanations disagree on this point, and the study is designed to compare them. The investigators plan to enroll 176 healthy adults, 18 to 45 years old, with a body mass index between 18 and 34. People will not be eligible if they cannot safely have an MRI scan, are actively trying to lose weight or taking weight-loss medication, have a history of a taste, smell, or eating disorder, or have an active neurological condition.

The main question it aims to answer is: Do children attending an emergency dental visit (because of dental pain, abscess, facial swelling, or dental trauma) have higher dental anxiety scores than children attending a routine dental visit?

Researchers will also look at whether dental anxiety is related to age, sex, previous dental visits, previous local anesthesia, and tooth decay experience.

Participants will:

* Have a parent or guardian fill out a short form about the child's age, sex, and dental history
* Receive a routine dental examination to record tooth decay (dmft/DMFT index)
* Answer the 4-question Turkish version of the Corah Dental Anxiety Scale during a single visit

No extra treatment or intervention is given as part of this study.

brief_summary:
This study evaluates whether treating severe obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) with continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) for approximately 6 months modifies local hippocampal and frontal cortex gray matter volume and blood-brain barrier (BBB) permeability in elderly men. Twenty-five men aged 70 years or older with newly diagnosed, previously untreated severe OSA (apnea-hypopnea index \[AHI\] \> 30) are compared with 25 age- and body-mass-index-matched control men without OSA (AHI \< 10, oxygen desaturation index \< 10).

All participants undergo a comprehensive neurocognitive assessment, instrumented gait and balance analysis, blood and urine sampling for systemic inflammatory and aquaporin markers, and a multimodal brain MRI with intravenous Gadolinium injection to quantify BBB permeability and gray/white matter volume. Patients repeat the MRI, cognitive testing, and gait/balance assessment after approximately 6 months of CPAP therapy, once adequate treatment adherence (≥5 hours/night).

The main hypothesis is that severe untreated OSA is associated with focal BBB permeability abnormalities in the hippocampus and frontal cortex, and that effective CPAP treatment partially reverses these anatomical and functional changes, together with improvements in executive/memory performance, gait, balance, and systemic inflammation. Results are expected to clarify the neurocognitive impact of OSA in the elderly, help target patients who most need treatment, and identify complementary pharmacological targets.
interventions: Multimodal brain MRI with Gadolinium injection
lead_sponsor: Centre Hospitalier Universitaire de Saint Etienne
primary_outcomes: Blood-brain barrier (BBB) permeability abnormality in the hippocampus and frontal cortex
title: Impact of Continuous Positive Airway Pressure Therapy on Bilateral Local Hippocampal Gray Matter Volume in Elderly Patients With Obstructive Sleep Apnea - Study BBBSAS

brief_summary: Lung cancer is the malignant tumor with the highest incidence and mortality rates in China. Malignant pleural effusion (MPE) is one of its most common complications, affecting approximately 15%-50% of patients with non-small cell lung cancer at initial diagnosis or during disease progression and indicating advanced-stage disease with a median survival of only 3-12 months. This study aims to establish the first large-scale, multicenter LC-MPE disease-specific cohort, integrating clinical, imaging, pleural fluid laboratory, pathological and genomic multimodal data to develop an AI-assisted model for the differential diagnosis of benign versus malignant MPE and a prognostic prediction model for LC-MPE patients. The study comprises a retrospective phase (3,000 patients diagnosed between January 2022 and September 2026) and a prospective phase (200 patients diagnosed between October 2026 and October 2028). The primary endpoint is overall survival (OS); secondary endpoints include pleural effusion progression-free survival (PE-PFS), duration of pleural effusion control, and 60-day and 30-day MPE recurrence rates. This observational study does not interfere with routine clinical care and strictly protects the personal information of participants.

brief_summary:
Episiotomy is a surgical cut made in the perineum, the area between the vagina and anus, during vaginal childbirth. Repairing an episiotomy can cause pain, and adequate pain relief is important for maternal comfort during and after delivery.

This study will compare two methods of providing anesthesia during episiotomy repair in women undergoing vaginal delivery with a mediolateral episiotomy at the Department of Maternal and Child Health (MCH), Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (PIMS), Islamabad, Pakistan.

A total of 80 eligible women will be enrolled and randomly assigned in equal numbers to two groups. The intervention group will receive a bilateral pudendal nerve block in addition to routine episiotomy repair and standard postpartum pain relief. The control group will receive conventional local anesthetic infiltration around the episiotomy area, along with routine repair and standard postpartum pain relief.

Pain will be assessed using a 100-mm Visual Analogue Scale (VAS), on which 0 represents no pain and 100 represents the worst imaginable pain. Pain will be assessed during episiotomy repair and at 1, 3, and 6 hours after delivery.

The study will also compare the need for additional pain medication, pain during sitting and walking, patient comfort and satisfaction, the duration of episiotomy repair, the need for additional local anesthetic, and complications associated with the procedures.

The aim is to determine whether pudendal nerve block provides better pain relief during episiotomy repair and improves early postpartum comfort compared with conventional local anesthetic infiltration.
lead_sponsor: Shaheed Zulfiqar Ali Bhutto Medical University
primary_outcomes: Pain intensity during episiotomy repair
title: Pudendal Nerve Block for Pain Relief During Episiotomy Repair: A Randomized Controlled Trial

brief_summary:
Objective: This study aims to investigate the effects of head-mounted display (HMD)-based interactive virtual reality simulation, an innovative educational technology in nursing education, on nursing students' skill performance, anxiety levels, satisfaction, and self-confidence during ice pack application.

Methods: This study is designed as a randomized controlled trial. The study population will consist of undergraduate nursing students enrolled at a public university in northeastern Türkiye during the 2026-2027 academic year. Based on a statistical power analysis, a total of 90 nursing students will be recruited and randomly assigned to either the experimental group (n = 45) or the control group (n = 45). Students in the experimental group will perform ice pack application using an HMD-based interactive virtual reality simulation, whereas students in the control group will perform the same procedure using a low-fidelity training mannequin. Data will be collected using the Student Information Form, Ice Pack Application Skills Checklist, Student Satisfaction and Self-Confidence in Learning Scale (SCLS), and Spielberger State-Trait Anxiety Inventory (STAI). Statistical analyses will be performed using SPSS version 25.0. Ethical approval (15.04.2026/07) institutional permission have been obtained. Both verbal and written informed consent will be obtained from all participants before their inclusion in the study.
primary_outcomes: Ice Pack Application Skill Performance Score
title: HMD-Based Virtual Reality Simulation in Nursing Skills Education

brief_summary:
Background:

Fish oils contain omega-3 fatty acids that play important roles in the body. Researchers are studying a new type of fish oil that contains very-long-chain omega-3 fatty acids (VLCPUFAs). They want to learn how this fish oil affects omega-3 levels in the blood and other measures related to health.

Objective:

To learn how a VLCPUFA-enriched fish oil changes omega-3 levels in the blood compared with a standard fish oil.

Eligibility:

Healthy adults ages 18 to 60 years with a body mass index (BMI) between 18 and 30 kg/m\^2 may be eligible.

Design:

Participants will take part in the study for about 28 to 30 weeks and will have approximately 4 to 5 clinic visits plus a follow-up phone call.

Participants will complete screening tests to determine whether they are eligible. These may include a physical examination, blood tests, measurement of height and weight, visual testing, cognitive testing, and questions about their diet, exercise, medications, and daily habits.

Participants will take 2 fish oil capsules by mouth every day for 8 weeks. They will then stop taking study capsules for about 12 weeks. After that, they will take a different fish oil capsule for another 8 weeks.

One fish oil contains very-long-chain omega-3 fatty acids (VLCPUFAs), and the other contains standard omega-3 fatty acids. Participants will not know which type they are taking during each study period.

Blood samples and other study assessments will be collected at the beginning and end of each treatment period to measure changes in omega-3 levels and other study markers.

Participants will receive a follow-up phone call about one week after taking their last dose of study supplement.
lead_sponsor: National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute (NHLBI)
primary_outcomes: Change in Omega-3 Index

brief_summary: For the pilot study, thirty eligible participants will be provided a concussion goody bag at their initial concussion evaluation visit. Each goody bag consists of 12 items, with a letter briefly describing the intended purpose for each item. Each participant will listen to a scripted tutorial by the research personnel, explaining the goody bag and why they are receiving it. Per standard of care, participants will return to clinic within 1-2 weeks for a follow up visit, at which time, they will complete a short questionnaire to assess overall usefulness of the bag, as well as individual rankings on how often they used each specific item. If the participant did not use any items, they will complete an additional question, describing why that item was not used, for each unused item. Also, the participants will be asked if they felt any additional items would have been helpful to them. Investigators expect these questionnaires to provide valuable insight from our patient perspectives about post-concussion care.

title: Tenapanor in Maintenance Hemodialysis Patients

brief_summary:
Background:

Waldenstrom macroglobulinemia (WM) is a type of blood cancer. It causes the blood to get thicker, which slows circulation and makes it harder to carry oxygen and other substances around the body. WM is treated with drugs called Bruton tyrosine kinase inhibitors (BTKi). But WM never goes away completely, and sometimes it gets worse despite treatment.

Objective:

To test a new drug (epcoritamab) in people with WM.

Eligibility:

People aged 18 years or older who have WM. They must have been taking a BTKi for a year or more.

Design:

Participants will be screened. They will have blood and urine tests. They will have imaging scans and a test of their heart function. They may have a bone marrow biopsy: A large needle will be used to remove a sample of the soft tissue and fluids from inside the hip bone.

Epcoritamab is injected under the skin, normally on the lower belly or thigh. Participants will be treated in 28-day cycles. They will have 12 treatment cycles. During the first cycle, they will come to the clinic to get an injection once a week for 4 weeks. After that, they will get 1 injection on the first day of each cycle.

Blood tests and imaging scans will be repeated at study visits. A saliva sample will be taken for genetic testing. Participants will also continue their normal treatment with BTKi.

After their last treatment with the study drug, participants will have 5 follow-up visits in 6 months. Tests, including a bone marrow biopsy, may be repeated. Follow-up visits will continue every 6 months for 3 (Omega) years or more.
lead_sponsor: National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute (NHLBI)
primary_outcomes: Rate of complete remission (CR) or very good partial remission (VGPR)
title: Epcoritamab as Consolidative Therapy for Waldenstr(SqrRoot)(Delta)m Macroglobulinemia (WM) Treated With a Bruton Tyrosine Kinase Inhibitor (BTKi)

Children with ADHD often experience challenges in social functioning, emotional regulation, and peer relationships. This trial will compare the difference in phenylalanine metabolism between the ketone monoester and control conditions. Secondary outcomes including plasma amino acid, plasma insulin, plasma glucose, capillary blood beta-hydroxybutyrate concentrations and whole body myofibrillar protein breakdown rate (k) will be explored as secondary measures. brief_summary: This prospective observational study aims to evaluate the acute effects of ketamine and propofol sedation on optic nerve sheath diameter (ONSD) in adult patients undergoing procedural sedation in the emergency department. ONSD is a noninvasive ultrasonographic measurement that may reflect changes in intracranial pressure. Adult patients who receive intravenous ketamine or propofol for procedural sedation will be included. The sedative agent will be selected by the treating physician according to routine clinical practice, and patients will not be randomly assigned to treatment groups. ONSD will be measured using ocular ultrasonography before and after sedation. The primary purpose of the study is to compare changes in ONSD following ketamine and propofol administration and to evaluate whether these commonly used sedative agents have different effects on ONSD.
primary_outcomes: Change in Optic Nerve Sheath Diameter (ONSD) From Baseline to 5 Minutes After Sedation

brief_summary:
The purpose of this phase II trial is to assess the clinical utility of clomiphene citrate for the augmentation of testosterone in prostate cancer survivors who complete androgen deprivation therapy (ADT), including the efficacy and tolerability of clomiphene, patient-reported quality of life outcomes, metabolic effects, biomarkers of response, and the oncologic safety of increasing testosterone.

Up to 83 eligible participants who have completed radiation and ADT for non-metastatic prostate cancer will participate in this study. Participants are assigned to one of two cohorts: Cohort A is comprised intermediate-risk survivors who underwent short-course ADT (4-17 mo.) and are hypogonadal ≥6 months after ending ADT, and Cohort R is comprised of survivors who recovered to eugonadal levels of testosterone (≥ 300 ng/dL) within 6 months after ending ADT.

Participants will be evaluated for clinical findings, toxicities, laboratory abnormalities (CBC, CMP, Lipid panel, Hgb A1C), changes to the hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal axis (E2, LH, FSH, TT) \[dependent on Cohort\], biochemical recurrence (PSA), and quality of life (FACT-P, FACT-Fatigue, qADAM).

Cohort R is an observational natural-recovery control group and will not be treated. Cohort A will be treated with oral clomiphene citrate, 25 mg, once daily for 6 months, then tested for persistence of response (eugonadal testosterone) after a 1-month washout period.

After completing study assessments, participants will transition to standard survivorship follow-up. Thereafter, long-term health outcomes will be reviewed to determine the rates of biochemical recurrence and metastasis after 5 years.
primary_outcomes: To evaluate the proportion of participants with eugonadal serum testosterone (≥ 300 ng/dL).
title: HRT-PC Trial: Hormone Recovery After Treatment for Prostate Cancer Trial. An Open-label Phase II Study of Clomiphene Citrate in Patients With Persistent Hypogonadism After ADT for Treatment of Localized Prostate Cancer

brief_summary: This prospective, randomized, comparative clinical study aims to compare the effectiveness of ultrasound-guided corticosteroid and tenoxicam injections in patients with lateral epicondylitis. A total of 72 participants will be randomized into two groups. One group will receive an ultrasound-guided methylprednisolone injection and the other group will receive an ultrasound-guided tenoxicam injection. Participants will be evaluated at baseline and at 4 and 12 weeks after treatment. Clinical outcomes will include pain, upper extremity function, lateral epicondylitis-related disability, and grip strength. Ultrasonographic assessment, including tendon thickness and strain elastography, will also be performed to evaluate structural and mechanical changes in the common extensor tendon.
primary_outcomes: Change From Baseline in Activity-Related Pain Intensity (VAS) at 12 Weeks
title: Comparative Effectiveness of Ultrasound-Guided Tenoxicam and Corticosteroid Injections for Lateral Epicondylitis

brief_summary:
This single-center, prospective, parallel-group randomized controlled trial will evaluate whether adding ultrasound-guided bilateral single-shot pecto-intercostal fascial plane block (PIFB) to standard multimodal systemic analgesia reduces the incidence of clinically significant chronic poststernotomy pain in adults undergoing elective isolated coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) through median sternotomy.

A total of 180 eligible participants will be randomized in a 1:1 ratio to either standard general anesthesia with standardized multimodal systemic analgesia alone or the same perioperative analgesic regimen with the addition of bilateral PIFB performed after induction of general anesthesia and before surgical incision. In the PIFB group, 15 mL of 0.25% bupivacaine will be administered on each side under ultrasound guidance. Perioperative anesthesia, systemic analgesia, rescue analgesia, intensive care management, and routine postoperative care will otherwise be standardized between groups.

The primary outcome will be the proportion of participants with clinically significant chronic poststernotomy pain on postoperative day 90. This outcome will be defined as pain that develops or worsens after surgery, is localized to the sternotomy line or related thoracic surgical areas, persists or recurs at 3 months, has an average intensity of at least 3 on a 0-10 Numeric Rating Scale during the preceding 7 days, and is not better explained by another clinical condition.

Secondary outcomes will include early postoperative pain intensity, acute pain burden, opioid consumption, rescue analgesic requirements, time to first rescue analgesia, postoperative nausea and vomiting, time to extubation, duration of mechanical ventilation, intensive care unit and hospital length of stay, and persistent postoperative pain at day 30. Participants will be followed through postoperative day 90.
primary_outcomes: Incidence of Clinically Significant Chronic Poststernotomy Pain
title: Bilateral Pecto-Intercostal Fascial Plane Block for Prevention of Chronic Poststernotomy Pain After CABG

brief_summary:
OLIGYNE-10 RT is an international registry of adults with gynecologic cancer and a limited number of active sites of cancer spread who receive radiotherapy to at least one metastatic lesion during routine care. The registry combines information from existing medical records with information collected prospectively. Treating clinical teams choose radiotherapy, imaging, systemic treatment, and follow-up. The registry does not assign treatment or require additional imaging or visits.

The classical cohort includes people with 1 to 5 active metastatic lesions assessed by computed tomography (CT) or magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), with or without positron emission tomography (PET). An extended, exploratory cohort includes people with 6 to 10 active metastatic lesions assessed by qualifying FDG PET/CT or FDG PET/MRI. Eligible cancers include cervical, endometrial and other uterine cancers, uterine sarcomas, ovarian and fallopian tube cancers, primary peritoneal cancers, vulvar and vaginal cancers, and other eligible rare gynecologic cancers.

The main objective is to describe the time from the first qualifying radiotherapy session or brachytherapy application until imaging shows cancer progression at any site or the participant dies. Other objectives include describing the control of treated lesions, patterns of cancer progression, survival, side effects, subsequent treatment of metastases, and how radiotherapy relates to the continuation or change of systemic treatment.

The initial target is 500 participants, with possible expansion to at least 1,000. Follow-up is planned for up to five years using information available from routine care.

brief_summary:
CAD is driven by atherosclerosis in the coronary arteries and is a major cause of myocardial infarction, heart failure, arrhythmias, and premature death. Despite contemporary secondary prevention including lipid lowering, revascularization when indicated, and antiplatelet therapy, participants with established CAD, particularly those post-ACS, remain at clinically meaningful residual risk of recurrent atherothrombotic events.

Intensifying antithrombotic therapy can reduce ischemic events but typically increases bleeding, as exemplified by the addition of low dose rivaroxaban to aspirin in stable atherosclerotic disease. This persistent efficacy-safety trade-off supports development of antithrombotic approaches that reduce pathological thrombosis while preserving hemostasis.

RBD1119 is a GalNAc-conjugated siRNA that targets factor XI mRNA in hepatocytes. The GalNAc moiety binds the asialoglycoprotein receptor on hepatocyte surfaces, enabling receptor mediated endocytosis and preferential hepatic uptake. Once internalized, RBD1119 mediates cleavage of factor XI mRNA via the RNA interference pathway, reducing hepatic factor XI expression and lowering circulating factor XI levels.

This multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase II trial will evaluate the PD, safety, and PK of subcutaneously administered RBD1119 in participants with stable coronary artery disease (CAD).
primary_outcomes: Primary objective
Primary endpoint
title: RBD1119 in Coronary Artery Disease (CAD)

brief_summary:
After spontaneous intracerebral haemorrhage (ICH), many survivors have persistent weakness of the arm and hand. Virtual reality (VR) training with haptic (force-feedback) devices may support upper-limb recovery, but evidence comes mainly from ischaemic or mixed stroke populations.

This exploratory substudy of the CrossReg-4-Health cohort will include 100 adults with upper-limb motor impairment after ICH. All participants will receive conventional physiotherapy and occupational therapy (ten 60-minute sessions over two weeks). Half will additionally receive 15 minutes of supervised haptic-assisted VR training per session using the Bimeo PRO system. Upper-limb motor function, disability, adherence, tolerability and adverse events will be assessed before and after the two-week programme to estimate feasibility and preliminary effect sizes for future trials.
primary_outcomes: Change in Fugl-Meyer Assessment - Upper Extremity (FMA-UE) motor score
title: Haptic-Assisted Virtual Reality Upper-Limb Rehabilitation After Intracerebral Haemorrhage

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to improve the combined use of PET/CT and MRI for imaging of the breast. PET/CT and MRI are usually performed in different body positions, which can change the shape and position of the breast and make it difficult to accurately align findings between the two examinations.

The main questions this study aims to answer are:

Can dedicated breast positioning during PET/CT reduce differences in breast shape and position compared with MRI?

Can image registration methods further improve the alignment of PET/CT and MRI images of the breast?

How accurately can findings seen on PET/CT be transferred to the corresponding location on MRI?

Participants in this study are breast cancer patients who are already scheduled to undergo PET/CT and PET/MRI as part of their clinical care. As part of the study, they will undergo an additional low-dose CT scan and an additional PET acquisition in a dedicated prone breast position. The additional PET images will be acquired using the tracer that has already been administered for the clinically indicated PET examination; no additional tracer injection is required.

The imaging data will then be used to develop and evaluate different methods for aligning PET/CT and MRI images of the breast.

The study does not investigate a new drug or treatment.
primary_outcomes: Target Registration Error After Multimodal Breast Image Registration
Mean Three-Dimensional Structural Similarity Index (3D-SSIM) Between Registered PET Datasets
title: Improving Combined PET/CT and MRI of the Breast Using Dedicated Breast Positioning and Image Registration

brief_summary:
Climate is the usual weather pattern of a place over a long time. Climate change means long-term shifts in climate, caused by natural processes and, above all, by human activity. Since the Industrial Revolution, factories and production have released more greenhouse gases into the air, and the planet has become warmer.

These changes are a risk to public health. They harm some groups more than others: children, older adults, people with long-term illnesses, and people with fewer resources. This makes health inequalities worse, so fighting climate change is a public health issue as well as an environmental one.

Young people today are more aware of climate change, which is a good chance to strengthen programs that protect and improve health. The few studies available show that climate change education for teenagers is mostly given in 7th and 8th grade. However, we do not know enough about whether this education changes behavior or improves health.

This study aims to find out how a climate change education program affects teenagers' climate literacy (their understanding of climate change) and their health-protective behaviors.

The study is quasi-experimental, with a control group and tests before and after the program. It will take place in two middle schools in Üsküdar, Istanbul, from September 2026 to January 2027. Participants will be 7th and 8th grade students from these schools.

The sample size was calculated with the G\*Power 3.1.9.4 program. Allowing for dropouts, we plan to include 154 teenagers: 77 in the education group and 77 in the control group.

Data will be collected with three tools: a Descriptive Information Form, the Climate Literacy Scale, and the Climate Change Health-Protective Behaviors Scale - Adolescent.
interventions: a climate change education for students in secondary school.
primary_outcomes: The Effect of Climate Change Education on Climate Literacy and Health-Protective Behaviors in Adolescents
title: A Climate Change Education Program for 7th and 8th Grade Students in Istanbul Schools: Does It Improve Climate Knowledge and Health-Protective Behaviors?

brief_summary:
Chest pain is among the most common reasons people attend an emergency department, and the electrocardiogram (ECG) recorded at triage is the first test used to decide who needs urgent treatment for a blocked coronary artery. Recognising the ECG patterns that indicate an acutely blocked artery is difficult. Many such patterns do not produce the classic ST-segment elevation, and identifying them reliably requires a level of ECG expertise that is not always available at the point of triage - particularly at night and among clinicians who are not cardiologists.

Artificial intelligence (AI) models that read the 12-lead ECG have been shown in several retrospective studies, mainly from Western Europe and the United States, to identify acute coronary occlusion more sensitively than conventional interpretation. These models are now in clinical use in a number of health systems. Their performance has not been assessed in a prospectively enrolled, unselected Slovenian emergency department population, and diagnostic accuracy commonly declines when a model is applied outside the setting in which it was developed.

TRIACS is a prospective, single-centre, observational external validation study in the Emergency Department of University Medical Centre Maribor. All consecutive adults presenting with symptoms suggestive of acute coronary syndrome who have a 12-lead ECG recorded at triage as part of routine care will be enrolled. Each triage ECG is analysed by the AI model. The model's output is withheld from all treating clinicians and plays no part in patient care; every patient receives standard guideline-directed management.

The main aim is to measure how accurately the AI model identifies angiographically confirmed occlusion myocardial infarction in this population, and to compare its accuracy with the triage decision actually made by the clinical team. The study is therefore designed to inform an adoption decision in either direction, rather than to demonstrate a predetermined conclusion.
primary_outcomes: Diagnostic accuracy of the AI-ECG model for angiographically confirmed occlusion myocardial infarction
title: AI-ECG Detection of Occlusion Myocardial Infarction at Emergency Department Triage (TRIACS)

brief_summary: The pain associated with endometriosis reflects a multifactorial pathophysiology combining peripheral nociception, central sensitisation and psychosocial factors. Although surgery is an integral part of treatment, a significant proportion of patients experience persistent pain several months after the procedure. To date, postoperative pain trajectories after endometriosis surgery remain poorly characterised, and there are no reliable predictors of chronic postoperative pain (CPP). This prospective, single-centre, longitudinal study aims to identify distinct postoperative pain trajectories and to assess whether perioperative quantitative sensory testing can predict the development of chronic postoperative pain at 3 and 6 months. Patients will undergo perioperative mechanical and pressure tests, including assessment of temporal summation and pressure pain thresholds, combined with validated measures of patient- reported outcomes. Follow-up assessments will be conducted on day 2, day 14, 1 month, 3 months, and 6 months after surgery to capture the dynamic evolution of pain, quality of life, fatigue, sexual function, and central sensitisation symptoms.

brief_summary:
Osteoporotic vertebral compression fractures are common and painful, especially in older adults. A minimally invasive surgery called vertebral augmentation is often used to relieve pain and stabilize the spine. Diabetes is also very common in these patients. However, it is unclear if having diabetes, especially with poor blood sugar control, makes it harder for patients to recover after this surgery.

This is a retrospective study. We will review the medical records of patients who had this spine surgery at our hospital between 2022 and 2024. We will look at patients with and without diabetes. We will compare their pain levels, physical function, and whether they experienced new fractures in the two years after surgery. We will use standard statistical methods to analyze this data. No new treatments or tests will be given to patients; we are only looking at past medical records. Patient privacy will be strictly protected.

This study will help doctors understand how diabetes affects recovery after spine surgery. The results may help guide better blood sugar management and bone health treatments for future patients with diabetes and spinal fractures.
lead_sponsor: The First Affiliated Hospital, Guangzhou University of Traditional Chinese Medicine
primary_outcomes: Incidence of Symptomatic Adjacent Vertebral Refracture within 2 Years after surgery
title: Impact of Diabetes on Patients With Osteoporotic Vertebral Compression Fractures After Vertebral Augmentation: A Retrospective Cohort Study

brief_summary:
Painful diabetic peripheral neuropathy (DPN) is a frequent and disabling complication of diabetes that commonly causes persistent foot pain, sleep impairment, and decreased quality of life. While oral medications such as duloxetine are established treatment options, many patients experience incomplete pain control or encounter dose-limiting side effects. Perineural botulinum toxin type A (BTX-A) injection has emerged as an interventional approach designed to inhibit peripheral pain signaling with targeted, prolonged local effect.

The purpose of this study is to compare the efficacy and safety of a single session of ultrasound-guided perineural BTX-A injection versus standard daily oral duloxetine therapy in relieving foot pain in patients with painful diabetic peripheral neuropathy.

Participants will be randomly assigned to one of two groups using a double-dummy design to preserve blinding:

* Group B (Botulinum Toxin): Receives a single session of ultrasound-guided perineural botulinum toxin type A injection around the ankle nerves plus daily oral placebo tablets for 12 weeks.
* Group D (Duloxetine): Receives a single session of sham subcutaneous injection plus oral duloxetine tablets daily for 12 weeks (30 mg once daily for week 1, increased to 60 mg once daily for weeks 2-12).

Participants will be followed for 6 months to evaluate changes in foot pain intensity on the Visual Analogue Scale (VAS) at 1 week, 1 month, 3 months, and 6 months. The study will also assess objective peripheral nerve function through bilateral nerve conduction studies (NCS) at baseline and 6 months, alongside evaluations of neuropathic pain scores, sleep quality, quality of life, and adverse effects.
primary_outcomes: Change from Baseline in Foot Pain Intensity on the Visual Analogue Scale (VAS) at 6 Months
title: Perineural Botulinum Toxin Injection Versus Oral Duloxetine in Relief of Foot Pain in Painful Peripheral Diabetic Neuropathy

brief_summary:
This study aims to compare the effects of knee bracing and eccentric loading exercises on pain and functional ability in adults with acute pes anserine bursitis. Pes anserine bursitis is a condition affecting the inner side of the knee that can cause pain and difficulty with activities such as walking, climbing stairs, and standing up from a chair.

A total of 32 participants will be included in the study and divided into two groups. One group will receive a knee-bracing intervention, while the other group will participate in a structured exercise program involving eccentric loading and strengthening exercises for the muscles around the knee.

The bracing group will be instructed to wear a properly fitted medial-support knee brace for approximately 6-8 hours daily during weight-bearing activities. The exercise group will perform prescribed exercises three times per week for eight weeks, with exercise intensity adjusted according to individual tolerance.

Pain intensity and knee-related functional ability will be assessed using the Visual Analogue Scale (VAS) and the Western Ontario and McMaster Universities Osteoarthritis Index (WOMAC). Assessments will be conducted before treatment and at the planned follow-up visits to evaluate changes in symptoms and function.

The findings are intended to help determine which intervention provides greater improvement in pain and functional ability in people with acute pes anserine bursitis and may help guide physiotherapy treatment decisions.
primary_outcomes: Change in Pain Intensity Measured by the Visual Analogue Scale (VAS)
title: Comparison of Bracing and Eccentric Loading Exercises on Pain Modulation and Functional Improvement in Acute Pes Anserine Bursitis Patients

brief_summary:
Feeding difficulties, such as food selectivity and refusal to try new foods, are common among preschool children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD). These difficulties may affect children's dietary intake, eating habits, and daily activities.

The aim of this study was to evaluate whether an individualized nutrition education programme delivered to parents could improve feeding behaviours, dietary intake, sleep habits, physical activity, and quality of life in preschool children with ASD.

The study included 45 children aged 3-6 years, including 30 children with ASD and 15 typically developing children. Children with ASD were randomly assigned to either a nutrition education group or a control group. Parents in the education group received eight individual nutrition education sessions over 16 weeks, supported by weekly telephone counselling. The typically developing children participated as a separate comparison group and were not randomly assigned.

The researchers assessed children's dietary intake, feeding behaviours, sleep habits, growth, physical activity, and screen time before and after the 16-week study period. Parent-reported quality of life was also evaluated.
primary_outcomes: Change in Feeding Behaviors Assessed by the Behavioral Pediatrics Feeding Assessment Scale (BPFAS)
title: Individualized Parent-Based Nutrition Education in Preschool Children With Autism Spectrum Disorder

brief_summary:

A total of 70 study participants are planned to be enrolled (the sample size requirement will be satisfied if the final valid dataset includes no fewer than 60 participants). The study aims to explore the effects of 12-week product intervention on glucose and lipid metabolism, body composition, and indicators related to metabolic syndrome.

This study adopts a double-blind design. All study participants will be randomly assigned into two groups. One group will receive the investigational product, a solid beverage containing postbiotics BPL1, \*Aronia melanocarpa\* fruit extract, apple polyphenols, D-allulose, inulin, lutein and other ingredients. The other group will receive the placebo control, a solid beverage identical to the investigational product in appearance, taste and packaging but without the above active ingredients.
primary_outcomes: Change in Metabolic Syndrome Risk Index (MetS)
title: Effects of a 12-Week Solid Beverage Intervention on Suboptimal Health Status
