brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to evaluate whether microencapsulated sodium propionate can modulate the gut microbiota and improve inflammatory and immunological parameters in adult patients with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) in remission or with mild disease activity. The study will also compare its effects with those of sodium butyrate.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Does sodium propionate modify gut microbiota composition and metabolic pathways in patients with IBD?
* Does sodium propionate influence inflammatory markers, immune cell balance (Treg/Th17), and quality of life?

Researchers will compare sodium propionate to sodium butyrate to determine whether propionate provides similar or additional benefits in microbiota modulation and inflammation control.

Participants will:

* Take either microencapsulated sodium propionate or sodium butyrate daily for 45 days, followed by a washout period and crossover to the alternate treatment
* Provide stool samples for microbiota analysis and blood samples for inflammatory cytokine assessment at predefined time points
* Complete quality-of-life questionnaires (IBDQ) during the study period
primary_outcomes: Change in Gut Microbiota Composition
title: Microencapsulated Sodium Propionate in IBD Microbiota Modulation

brief_summary:
Many pregnant women in India use mobile phones to get health information. Nivi runs a free WhatsApp service called askNivi that answers questions about pregnancy and sends reminders about prenatal care visits.

The current version of askNivi replies using a set of prepared answers. This study tests a new version that uses artificial intelligence to write replies. The new version looks up information in a reviewed collection of maternal health materials before answering, so its replies stay grounded in checked sources. It is also designed to recognize symptoms that may signal a pregnancy complication and to tell the user to seek care right away.

Women who join the study are assigned at random to one of the two versions. Neither version replaces medical care, and both send the same weekly messages and clinic reminders. Women can ask questions at any time throughout their pregnancy.

The study will look at how much women use each version, how useful they find it, how they decide when to seek care, and whether they attend prenatal care visits. About 2,500 pregnant women in Assam, Madhya Pradesh, and Uttar Pradesh will take part. Participation lasts from enrollment, between 10 and 20 weeks of pregnancy, until delivery.
primary_outcomes: Percentage of weeks with any user interaction
Mean conversational turns per week
Mean number of substantive user queries per week
Percentage of weeks with any substantive user query
title: Comparing AI and Standard Pregnancy Chatbots

brief_summary:
Critically ill patients can develop high levels of inflammation, which may contribute to organ damage, muscle loss, and difficulty recovering physical function. Fish oil contains omega-3 fatty acids that may help reduce inflammation. However, the most suitable dose of fish oil given intravenously (directly into a vein) in critically ill patients with high levels of inflammation is uncertain.

The FOiL-INFLAMe trial is a phase II study comparing two doses of intravenous fish oil with usual care. Its main purpose is to determine their effects on inflammation and assess their safety, to help select a dose for a larger trial. The study will also examine organ function, muscle mass, physical function, and clinical outcomes.

The study will enrol 159 critically ill adults who require breathing support, receive nutrition through a feeding tube, and have high blood levels of interleukin-6 (IL-6), a marker of inflammation. Participants will be assigned by chance to one of three groups:

(i) Lower-dose fish oil: 0.2 grams per kilogram of body weight per day. (ii) Higher-dose fish oil: 0.4 grams per kilogram of body weight per day. (iii) Usual care without additional intravenous fish oil.

All groups will receive usual intensive care and nutritional support. In the fish oil groups, treatment will begin within six hours of group assignment and will be given intravenously over eight hours each day, for up to seven days while in the intensive care unit.

The main outcome is the change in blood IL-6 levels from day 1 to day 4. We will also measure other blood markers, assess organ function, use ultrasound to measure thigh muscle size, and assess handgrip strength and short physical performance battery test. Other outcomes include survival, time on mechanical ventilation, and length of intensive care and hospital stay. Participants will be monitored for potential side effects throughout treatment.
primary_outcomes: Change in blood interleukin-6 (IL-6) concentration from Day 1 to Day 4
title: Intravenous Fish Oil Emulsion in Critically Ill Patients With High Inflammatory Status.

brief_summary:
Traumatic injuries can cause severe bleeding, which causes a lot of deaths worldwide that could be prevented. Starting treatment as early as possible has been shown to improve survival, which makes fast care very important. This could mean that giving blood products (like red blood cells and plasma) before patients are transported to the hospital might improve survival. However, research from other countries has shown mixed results concerning the effectiveness of giving blood before the patient has arrived in the hospital as a treatment for bleeding patients.

In the Netherlands, the helicopter emergency services supports the ambulance teams in life threatening situations. There are four helicopter services spread across the Netherlands. Among other things they can administer red blood cells and two out of four helicopter emergency service teams can give plasma as well.

Although other countries have studied their prehospital transfusion programs, no such research has been done in the Dutch system. This study aims to find out which transfusion strategy works best for adult trauma patients who might have severe bleeding after traumatic injuries in the Netherlands.

The goal of this observational study is to find out whether different blood-transfusion approaches used by the helicopter emergency services in the Netherlands helps survival in adult trauma patients with severe bleeding who are treated by the Dutch helicopter emergency services. The main question it aims to answer is: Does using different transfusion strategies change the chance of mortality in the first 24 hours?

Participants will receive the care they normally have. The helicopter emergency doctors will note information about the treatment they gave before the patient was transported to the hospital and the research will register information about the treatment and outcomes in the hospital.
primary_outcomes: All cause 24-hour mortality
title: Prehospital Transfusion Outcomes in Traumatic Hemorrhage: a Prospective Cohort Study

brief_summary:
The goal of this observational study is to learn if a computer program can tell what type of ovarian tumour a person has from a CT scan taken before surgery. The program uses artificial intelligence (AI). It sorts tumours into three groups:

* benign: not cancer
* borderline: abnormal cells that usually behave less aggressively than cancer
* malignant: cancer

Before surgery, doctors try to judge which group a tumour belongs to. This guides where and how the operation is done. This judgement is often hard, especially for borderline tumours. An AI program that does it well could help doctors plan surgery.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

* How well does the AI program sort ovarian tumours into benign, borderline and malignant on CT scans?
* Does the AI program work as well on scans from hospitals it did not learn from?

Researchers will compare the AI program's results with the final diagnosis from the tumour tissue removed during surgery. They will also compare the program with methods doctors use today, such as ultrasound-based risk scores and the radiologist's report. In a smaller group, researchers will test the program on MRI scans.

This study only uses information that already exists. It includes adults who had surgery for a mass in or near the ovary at hospitals in the Netherlands and Belgium. Researchers will use:

* CT or MRI scans made before surgery as part of regular care
* information from medical records
* the tissue diagnosis after surgery

Participants will not be contacted. They will not have any extra scans, tests or visits. Each hospital codes the data before sharing them, so researchers cannot see participants' names. The study does not change anyone's care.
primary_outcomes: Discrimination of the CADx model for three-class classification (benign, borderline, malignant): macro-averaged AUROC
title: AI Analysis of CT Scans to Classify Ovarian Tumours as Benign, Borderline or Malignant Before Surgery

brief_summary:
This study will explore whether non-invasive electrical stimulation can reduce chronic genital pain, deep pelvic pain, or both in adult women whose symptoms have persisted for at least six months despite conventional treatment.

Approximately 50 women will participate at several clinical centers. After recording their pain for two weeks, participants will use a portable electrical stimulation device at home for 12 weeks. Two adhesive electrodes will be placed on intact skin beside the vulva. Stimulation will be applied for 30 minutes twice daily, at an individually adjusted, comfortable intensity. No surgery or implantation is required.

The main outcome is the proportion of participants achieving at least a 30% reduction in their main pain symptom after 12 weeks. Researchers will also assess daily functioning, quality of life, pain medication use, and side effects. Follow-up assessments will take place three and six months after treatment ends.

All participants will receive stimulation; there is no comparison group. This exploratory study aims to assess safety, tolerability, and preliminary signs of benefit to guide a future controlled trial.
primary_outcomes: Change in Genital and/or Visceral Pelvic Pain Intensity
title: Transcutaneous Genital Nerves Stimulation for the Treatment of Refractory Chronic Pelvic and Genital Pain in Women.

brief_summary:
In cases of early pregnancy complicated with intrauterine adhesions (IUAs), termination of pregnancy is prone to incomplete abortion with retained gestational products, failed abortion or uterine perforation due to altered uterine cavity structure and gestational sac obscured by adhesive bands. Reoperation may even be required, which increases the risk of surgical trauma, as well as the psychological and financial burdens on patients. Meanwhile, some patients with IUAs still have fertility demands in the future, so the adhesions also need to be addressed.

Hysteroscopy allows direct visualization to remove intrauterine gestational contents, lowering the risks of tissue retention and reoperation. It also enables concurrent treatment of existing IUAs. Combined with postoperative interventions to prevent adhesion recurrence, this approach can restore the uterine cavity structure and endometrium, improve subsequent fertility, and reduce patients' psychological stress as well as the time and economic costs incurred by repeated hospital admissions and surgeries for IUAs.

This clinical controlled study aims to explore the clinical outcomes and advantages of hysteroscopy applied for termination of early pregnancy combined with simultaneous management of IUAs, so as to provide reliable evidence for the clinical application of combined hysteroscopic abortion and adhesiolysis in such patients. In addition, immunohistochemical detection of decidual tissues will be performed to analyze the influences of immune cell subsets, inflammatory markers, vascular remodeling-related markers and other indicators on the disease, offering references for its clinical management and treatment.

This is a prospective controlled study. Eligible patients diagnosed with early pregnancy complicated with IUAs who underwent pregnancy termination in the Family Planning Ward of our hospital will be enrolled from the date of ethical approval in accordance with the inclusion and exclusion criteria. Patients are divided into two groups: the experimental group receives hysteroscopic abortion combined with simultaneous adhesiolysis, and the control group undergoes ultrasound-guided artificial abortion.

After being fully informed of the pros and cons of both surgical procedures, patients will select their preferred operation voluntarily. General patient information will be recorded, including age, obstetric history, fetal viability of the current pregnancy, intraoperative blood loss, placement of anti-adhesive materials in the uterine cavity and postoperative estrogen administration. Postoperative follow-up will be conducted for 2 years after the enrollment of the last subject, with observed indicators including the rate of residual gestational tissue, recurrence rate of IUAs and subsequent pregnancy outcomes.

Appropriate statistical descriptive indicators and analytical methods will be selected based on the research objectives, data types and distribution characteristics. Statistical differences and clinical implications between the two surgical protocols will be compared and analyzed
interventions: Hysteroscopy adhesiolysis combined with vacuum aspiration
lead_sponsor: Women's Hospital School Of Medicine Zhejiang University
primary_outcomes: Rate of subsequent pregnancy after surgery
title: Comparison of Operative Hysteroscopy and Vacuum Aspiration for Terminating First-trimester Pregnancy With Intrauterine Adhesions

brief_summary: This study is a prospective, single-center, randomized, parallel-group, open-label clinical trial titled "Intervention with the 'Xu Xue Tong Luo Traditional Chinese Medicine Compound for Capecitabine-Related Hand-Foot Syndrome." The research hypothesis is that adding this traditional Chinese medicine hand and foot bath to standard baseline care will result in a significantly higher efficacy rate-defined as a ≥1-grade reduction in Hand-Foot Syndrome (HFS) severity after 3 weeks-compared to baseline care alone.The study plans to enroll 110 patients with capecitabine-related Grade 1-2 HFS (with some eligible Grade 3 patients), who will be randomized in a 1:1 ratio to the control group and the intervention group. The control group will receive standard baseline care; the intervention group will receive standard baseline care supplemented with a fixed 12-ingredient traditional Chinese medicine hand-and-foot bath, in which processed Aconite is pre-decocted to reduce toxicity. Patients will soak their hands and feet in the decoction at 38-41°C at least 4 times per week for 3 consecutive weeks.Primary endpoint: The proportion of patients with a ≥1-grade reduction in HFS score from baseline after 3 weeks of intervention.

brief_summary:
Spontaneous intracerebral haemorrhage (ICH) is a severe form of stroke with high mortality and frequent long-term disability. Current tools to predict how an individual patient will recover are limited.

CrossReg-4-Health is a prospective, multicentre observational cohort study that will enrol 300 consecutive adults with acute spontaneous ICH at three hospitals in Slovenia and Austria. During hospitalisation, the study will collect clinical data, standardised neurological and pain assessments, routine laboratory results, CT, CT angiography and MRI findings, and two research blood samples for biomarkers of brain injury, inflammation, coagulation and pain. Participants will be followed up at 6 and 12 months for survival, functional outcome, neurological status, pain, health-related quality of life, rehabilitation use and readmissions.

The main aim is to develop a multimodal prognostic model for functional outcome (modified Rankin Scale) 12 months after ICH.
primary_outcomes: Unfavourable functional outcome at 12 months (modified Rankin Scale 4-6)

brief_summary:
This study will compare the effectiveness and safety of topical clascoterone 1% cream and adapalene 0.1% cream in patients with mild-to-moderate acne vulgaris. Acne is a common skin condition that causes blackheads, whiteheads, pimples, and inflammation.

A total of 130 eligible participants aged 12-40 years will be enrolled in a randomized controlled trial at the Dermatology Outpatient Department of Pak Emirates Military Hospital, Rawalpindi, Pakistan. Participants will be randomly assigned to one of two treatment groups. Group A will receive clascoterone 1% cream applied twice daily, while Group B will receive adapalene 0.1% cream applied once daily at night.

Treatment will continue for 12 weeks. Participants will be assessed at baseline and during follow-up visits at Weeks 4, 8, and 12. Treatment response will be evaluated using the Investigator's Global Assessment (IGA) score and acne lesion counts. Treatment success will be defined as an IGA score of 0 (clear) or 1 (almost clear), with at least a two-grade improvement from baseline at Week 12. Adverse effects, treatment compliance, and patient satisfaction will also be assessed.

The study aims to compare the efficacy and tolerability of both treatments in patients with mild-to-moderate acne vulgaris.
primary_outcomes: Treatment success at week 12
title: Comparison of Topical Clascoterone 1% Cream Versus Adapalene 0.1% Cream in the Treatment of Mild-to-Moderate Acne Vulgaris: A Randomized Controlled Trial

brief_summary:
Spinal muscular atrophy (SMA) is an inherited neuromuscular disorder caused by mutations in the SMN1 gene, leading to motor neuron degeneration and progressive muscle atrophy. Despite recent advances in therapeutic options, the clinical management of SMA remains challenging due to the heterogeneity of disease progression and variability in treatment response.

This study aims to identify and validate novel biomarkers to improve the diagnosis, prognosis, and therapeutic monitoring of patients with SMA through a multi-omics and translational research approach.
primary_outcomes: Identification of biomarkers that distinguish patients with SMA from healthy controls and differentiate between disease phenotypes (p < 0.05).

title: Advanced Multi-omics and -System Approaches to Identify Novel Biomarkers for SMA

brief_summary: An accurate medical diagnosis depends on the doctor getting a complete picture of the patient's health story, but clinic visits are short. Before some cardiology appointments, patients may be able to speak with an artificial intelligence (AI) "interviewer" - through a secure web page, usually at home - about their symptoms, medications, allergies, medical history, and what they want their doctor to understand. The AI interviewer creates a written summary for the cardiologist. It does not make diagnoses, give treatment advice, or replace the doctor: the cardiologist still takes and verifies the medical history in the usual way, and nothing written by the AI goes into the medical record without the doctor's review. In this study, 60 adults attending a first or new cardiology consultation at London Health Sciences Centre University Hospital or the London Cardiac Institute will be invited to use the AI interviewer before their appointment. Patients who prefer not to take part receive usual care. We will measure how many participants complete the interview and have a summary ready before their visit, how long the interview and the visit take, whether patients find the interviewer easy to use and feel able to explain their concerns, whether cardiologists find the summaries useful and accurate, and whether any important errors or omissions occur. Every summary is checked by the treating cardiologist, and independent physicians review all concerning cases plus a random sample. Results will show whether this workflow is feasible and safe enough to justify a larger study.
lead_sponsor: London Health Sciences Centre Research Institute OR Lawson Research Institute of St. Joseph's
primary_outcomes: Usability
title: AI-CLINIC: A Prospective Multisite Feasibility and Safety Study of AI-Assisted Pre-Consultation History-Taking in Outpatient Cardiology

brief_summary:
This study will evaluate whether an expanded diagnostic strategy can reduce antibiotic use in patients aged 65 years or older who are hospitalized with community-acquired acute respiratory infection, without negatively affecting clinical outcomes.

The expanded diagnostic strategy combines multiplex respiratory polymerase chain reaction (PCR), serial procalcitonin measurements, and bedside lung ultrasound. The results of these tests will be integrated to support decisions about antibiotic treatment.

The study will compare the expanded diagnostic strategy with conventional diagnostic management. The main outcome will be the total duration of antibiotic therapy. The study will also assess the use of high-impact antibiotics, microbiological diagnosis, hospital and intensive care unit stay, complications, mortality, recurrence of infection, hospital readmissions, detection of multidrug-resistant microorganisms, and antibiotic-related adverse events.
primary_outcomes: Total Duration of Antibiotic Therapy
title: Expanded Diagnostic Strategy in Older Adults Hospitalized With Community-Acquired Acute Respiratory Infection

brief_summary: SBRT combined with dual PD-1/CTLA-4 blockade (iparomlimab and tuvonralimab, QL1706) and bevacizumab may provide complementary local and systemic antitumor activity in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). This prospective, single-arm, single-center study evaluates the efficacy and safety of stereotactic body radiotherapy (SBRT) to all intra- and extrahepatic lesions combined with QL1706 (7.5 mg/kg intravenously on day 1 every 3 weeks) and bevacizumab (15 mg/kg intravenously on day 1 every 3 weeks) in patients with inoperable locally advanced or oligometastatic HCC (BCLC stage B or C). All lesions receive SBRT at 8 Gy in 3-5 fractions completed within 30 days; systemic therapy starts within 1 week before or after the start of radiotherapy and continues as maintenance for up to 2 years, until progression, death, or unacceptable toxicity. The primary endpoint is objective response rate per RECIST 1.1. Secondary endpoints include complete response, disease control rate, time to response, duration of response, local control, progression-free survival, time to progression, and overall survival per RECIST 1.1 and mRECIST, safety per CTCAE v6.0, and quality of life per EORTC QLQ-C30 and QLQ-HCC18. A total of 33 patients will be enrolled at Beijing Cancer Hospital.
primary_outcomes: Objective Response Rate per RECIST 1.1
title: SBRT Combined With Iparomlimab and Tuvonralimab (QL1706) and Bevacizumab for Hepatocellular Carcinoma

brief_summary: This is a prospective, multicenter observational cohort study for patients with lung nodules suspicious for early-stage lung cancer. The study aims to build AI-assisted diagnostic models by integrating clinical data, CT imaging and multi-omics biomarkers, and validate a rapid evaluation system for bronchoscopic biopsy specimens. No investigational drugs or devices will be applied; all participants receive routine clinical care. We will collect clinical records, CT images, blood and tissue samples, and conduct long-term follow-up of disease outcomes. A total of 1050 subjects will be enrolled from 8 participating hospitals in China.
primary_outcomes: Sub-study 1:Area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of the multi-modal diagnostic model
Sub-study2:Area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of three-dimensional interference microscopy
title: Diagnostic Performance of an AI-Based Multi-Omics Model for Early Lung Cancer

brief_summary:
The goal of this observational study is to learn whether information about heart muscle tissue from preoperative photon-counting CT, a newer type of CT scan, can help predict heart recovery 3 months after coronary artery bypass surgery. The study will include adults aged 18 years or older with coronary artery disease who are scheduled for coronary artery bypass surgery without another major heart operation.

The main question it aims to answer is:

\- Can heart muscle information from CT before surgery help predict the amount of blood remaining in the heart's left pumping chamber after it contracts, adjusted for body size, 3 months after surgery? This measurement is called the left ventricular end-systolic volume index and will be used to assess early changes in heart structure after surgery.

Participants will:

* Have photon-counting CT scans and heart ultrasound examinations before surgery, within 7 days after surgery, and approximately 3 months after surgery.
* Have blood tests before surgery and within 7 days afterward to help researchers assess changes in heart muscle tissue.
* Provide information about medications, hospital admissions, and their health during follow-up.

Clinical doctors will determine surgery and treatment based on each participant's medical needs.
primary_outcomes: Left ventricular end-systolic volume index at 3 months after CABG
title: Prospective Study Protocol for Multiparametric PCCT Assessment of Early Ventricular Outcomes After CABG

brief_summary:
This study will compare benmelstobart plus anlotinib with sunitinib as the first treatment for adults with advanced non-clear cell renal cell carcinoma, a type of kidney cancer. Eligible participants have cancer that cannot be removed surgically, has returned locally, or has spread to other parts of the body. Patients with chromophobe, collecting duct, or renal medullary carcinoma are not eligible.

Benmelstobart is an immunotherapy that blocks PD-L1, a protein involved in suppressing the immune response to cancer. Anlotinib and sunitinib are targeted medicines that inhibit signals involved in tumor growth and blood vessel formation.

The study plans to enroll 126 participants at multiple centers. Participants will be randomly assigned in a 2:1 ratio to receive either benmelstobart plus anlotinib or sunitinib. Participants and study doctors will know which treatment is assigned.

The main purpose is to compare how long participants live without their cancer getting worse. The study will also assess tumor response, overall survival, side effects, and quality of life.
primary_outcomes: Progression-Free Survival (PFS)
title: Benmelstobart Plus Anlotinib Versus Sunitinib as First-Line Treatment for Advanced Non-Clear Cell Renal Cell Carcinoma

brief_summary: This study is a multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase II clinical trial designed to evaluate the efficacy, safety, and pharmacokinetic profile of SYH2066 tablets in adult patients with RSV infection. Approximately 80 adult patients with RSV infection are expected to be enrolled and assigned to three active treatment groups and one placebo group, with approximately 20 eligible participants per group. The study consists of a 3-day screening period, a 5-day treatment period, and an 8- to 10-day follow-up period. Throughout the study, safety assessments, PK blood sampling, nasopharyngeal (NP) swab collection, and RSV symptom recording will be performed
primary_outcomes: Area under the curve (AUC) of RSV RNA viral load measured by RT-qPCR in nasopharyngeal swab samples
title: Phase 2 Study of SYH2066 Tablets Compared With Placebo in Chinese Adult Patients With Respiratory Syncytial Virus Infection.

brief_summary: This study is designed as a single-blind, placebo-controlled, randomized, parallel-group trial. Subjects will be randomized in a 2:1 ratio to receive either NKS-3 or matching placebo, with a total planned enrollment of 31 subjects. During the 90-day treatment period, subjects will self-administer the assigned blinded study treatment daily at home. Given the exploratory nature of the study, which is intended to assess the feasibility of and generate preliminary evidence supporting the study hypothesis, a single-blind design has been selected. This approach reduces the logistical and organizational complexity associated with implementing a double-blind design while maintaining blinding of study participants to minimize expectation bias. Considering the exploratory objectives of the study, the selected design is considered appropriate and is not expected to compromise the scientific validity or the safety of participants.
interventions: Investigational product is a modified linoleic acid, named NKS-3. This non-caloric agent, synthetized from linoleic acid, is a fat taste receptors agonist, targeting CD36 with also an impact on GPR120
primary_outcomes: Evaluate the effect of NKS-3 compared with placebo on the percent change in body weight from baseline (V0) to Day 90 (V2) in adults with obesity.
title: A PHASE 2A, EXPLORATORY, RANDOMIZED, SINGLE-BLIND, PLACEBO-CONTROLLED STUDY TO EVALUATE THE EFFICACY OF WEIGHT LOSS INDUCED BY NKS-3 IN OBESE ADULTS.

brief_summary:
People who receive a donor kidney must take drugs to prevent their bodies from attacking the new organ. These drugs are called immunosuppressants. Probiotics are beneficial microbes that support gut health. They are often given to reduce immunosuppressant toxicity for the gut. The goal of this clinical trial is to learn if probiotics change the levels of immunosuppressants in the blood in patients who have received a kidney transplant.

The main question it aims to answer is:

• Does a short-term treatment with a probiotic mixture change the circulating levels of the immunosuppressant drugs cyclosporine A, tacrolimus, sirolimus, everolimus, mycophenolic acid, mycophenolate mofetil, and prednisolone? In addition, researchers will also see if probiotics reduce systemic inflammation or ameliorate renal function.

Study participants will be patients with kidney transplant. At different times, each participant will take either probiotics or look-alike capsules with no probiotics. Researchers will compare the levels of immunosuppressant in the blood when participants take the probiotics with those when they take the capsules with no microbes.

Study participants will have to:

* Take oral capsules containing a probiotc mixture for one month and look-alike capsules with no probiotics for another month with a one-month interval between these two treatments;
* Go to the hospital every 30 days for three months for the collection of blood samples;
* Collect feces specimens for microbiome analysis every 30 days for three months and bring them to the hospital.
primary_outcomes: Changes in immunosuppressant drug blood levels
title: Effect of Probiotics on Immunosuppressant Therapy in Kidney Transplant Recipients
